title: Additional Support Measures in Response to COVID-19 Pandemic
what_it_is: Additional Support Measures in Response to COVID-19 Pandemic

sections.label: WHO COVID-19 pandemic declaration
sections.summary: The WHO declared COVID-19 a pandemic on 11 March, with over 410,000 infected across more than 190 countries.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Three weeks after my Budget speech, on 11 March, the World Health Organization (WHO) declared COVID-19 a pandemic, recognising the severity and risk of further global spread.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Today, the WHO estimates that the number of people infected has exceeded 410,000, across more than 190 countries.

sections.label: S&P 500 fastest drop
sections.summary: The S&P 500 fell 30% from its peak in 22 trading days, the fastest drop of this magnitude in history.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The S&P 500 Index took only 22 trading days to fall by 30% from its peak, making it the fastest drop of this magnitude in history.

sections.label: Singapore GDP contraction and forecast
sections.summary: Singapore's economy contracted 10.6% quarter-on-quarter in the first quarter, and MTI downgraded 2020 growth forecast to -4.0% to -1.0%.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Based on advance Gross Domestic Product (GDP) estimates released this morning, in the first quarter, the Singapore economy contracted by 10.6% quarter-on-quarter, or 2.2% year-on-year, reversing the 0.6% growth in the previous quarter.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: This morning, the Ministry of Trade and Industry further downgraded Singapore's GDP growth forecast for 2020 from a range of -0.5% to 1.5% announced last month to between -4.0% and -1.0%.

sections.label: Resilience Budget and Past Reserves
sections.summary: Measures worth over $48 billion are introduced in the Resilience Budget, with up to $17 billion drawn from Past Reserves.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Today, I will introduce measures worth over $48 billion in this Resilience Budget to deal decisively with the situation at hand.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Altogether, we are dedicating close to $55 billion to support our people in this battle, amounting to 11% of our GDP.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The Government has sought and obtained the President's in-principle support to draw up to $17 billion from our Past Reserves to fund part of the Resilience Budget.

sections.label: Higher co-funding of wages
sections.summary: Government co-funding of wages for every local worker in employment will rise from 8% to 25%.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: For every local worker in employment, I will raise the Government's co-funding of wages from 8% to 25%.

sections.label: Jobs Support Scheme allocation
sections.summary: $15.1 billion will be allocated to support more than 1.9 million local employees under the Jobs Support Scheme.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: With these enhancements, a total of $15.1 billion will be allocated to support more than 1.9 million local employees under the Jobs Support Scheme.

sections.label: Support for self-employed persons
sections.summary: Sets aside $1.2 billion for self-employed persons and $48 million to extend the Self-Employed Person Training Support Scheme to December 2020, raising the hourly training allowance from $7.50 to $10 from 1 May 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Overall, we expect to reach out to most of the self-employed persons who depend on self-employment for their livelihood and have less means and family support.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: I will set aside $1.2 billion for this.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: I will also provide sustained support for self-employed persons to make full use of any downtime during this period to train and upskill.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: I will set aside another $48 million to extend the Self-Employed Person Training Support Scheme to December 2020, and enhance the hourly training allowance from $7.50 to $10, with effect from 1 May 2020.

sections.label: Enhanced Workfare Special Payment
sections.summary: Enhances the Workfare Special Payment, increasing the cash payout for this group of Workfare recipients to $3,000 each.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: In this Resilience Budget, I will enhance the Workfare Special Payment and increase the payout received by this group of Workfare recipients to $3,000 each, in cash.

sections.label: Traineeships and SGUnited Jobs
sections.summary: Workforce Singapore will co-share manpower costs for traineeships for local first-time jobseekers, supporting up to 8,000 traineeships, and the SGUnited Jobs initiative will create about 10,000 jobs over the next year.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Under this programme, Workforce Singapore (WSG) will co-share manpower costs with enterprises that offer traineeships targeted at local first-time jobseekers this year.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We are looking to support up to 8,000 traineeships this year, across both large and small enterprises.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: This will include science and technology traineeships in our R&D labs, deep-tech startups, accelerators and incubators.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: I will also launch the SGUnited Jobs initiative to create about 10,000 jobs over the next one year.

sections.label: Enhanced Care and Support Package
sections.summary: Triples the cash payout for all adult Singaporeans from $100 to $300 to a range of $300 to $900, depending on income.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: First, I will enhance the Care and Support Package announced in the Unity Budget.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: I will triple the cash payout for all adult Singaporeans from the earlier announced range of $100 to $300, to a range of $300 to $900, depending on income.

sections.label: Payouts for families
sections.summary: States that a young family will receive around $2,900 instead of $1,300, and a three-generation family about $6,700 instead of $1,800.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: With these enhancements, a young family will now receive around $2,900, instead of $1,300, under the Care and Support Package.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: A three-generation family will receive about $6,700, instead of $1,800.

sections.label: Cost of Care and Support Package
sections.summary: States that the enhanced Care and Support Package, with other Care and Support measures from the Unity Budget, will cost around $4.6 billion.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Together with the other Care and Support measures announced during the Unity Budget, the enhanced Care and Support Package will cost around $4.6 billion.

sections.label: Jobs Support and Wage Credit
sections.summary: The Jobs Support Scheme and Wage Credit Scheme will give businesses $16.2 billion by October, and income tax payments due in April, May and June 2020 will be deferred.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Altogether, the Jobs Support Scheme and Wage Credit Scheme will flow $16.2 billion into the hands of businesses by October this year.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: For companies, we will defer income tax payments due in April, May and June 2020.

sections.label: Self-employed income tax deferral
sections.summary: For self-employed persons, income tax payments due in May, June and July 2020 will be deferred.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: For self-employed persons, the payment cycle for personal income tax for the Year of Assessment (YA) 2020 generally starts in May 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We will defer the income tax payments due in May, June and July 2020.

sections.label: Property Tax relief for commercial properties
sections.summary: In 2020, qualifying commercial properties badly affected by COVID-19, including hotels, serviced apartments, tourist attractions, shops and restaurants, will pay no Property Tax.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: For 2020, qualifying commercial properties that have been more badly affected by the COVID-19 outbreak, including hotels, serviced apartments, tourist attractions, shops, and restaurants, will pay no Property Tax.

sections.label: Hawker centre rental waiver
sections.summary: NEA will give stallholders in hawker centres managed by NEA or NEA-appointed operators three months of rental waiver, up from one month announced in the Unity Budget.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: NEA will give stallholders in hawker centres managed by NEA or NEA-appointed operators three months of rental waiver, up from one month announced in the Unity Budget.

sections.label: Twenty billion loan capital
sections.summary: In addition to enhancements to financing schemes, $20 billion of loan capital will be set aside in this Budget.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: In addition to these enhancements to our financing schemes, I will set aside $20 billion of loan capital in this Budget.

sections.label: Airline revenue loss projection
sections.summary: The International Air Transport Association projected that COVID-19 will hit worldwide airline revenues by up to US$250 billion this year.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The International Air Transport Association projected that COVID-19 will hit worldwide airline revenues by up to US$250 billion this year.

sections.label: Passenger traffic and SIA capacity cuts
sections.summary: Daily passenger traffic fell over 90% by 24 March 2020, and SIA announced a 96% capacity cut to end-April across its network.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: As of 24 March 2020, daily passenger traffic has fallen by more than 90%.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The Singapore Airlines Group (SIA) has announced a 96% cut to their scheduled capacity up to end-April across their entire network.

sections.label: Hub industries GDP and employment
sections.summary: The hub and its adjacent industries contribute over 5% of Singapore's GDP and employ about 192,000 people.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The hub and its adjacent industries contribute over 5% of Singapore's GDP and employ approximately 192,000 people.

sections.label: Wage offset for local workers
sections.summary: For every local worker in employment, a total 75% wage offset is provided for the first $4,600 of monthly wages.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: For every local worker in employment, I will provide a total of 75% wage offset for the first $4,600 of monthly wages.

sections.label: Support for tourism and MICE
sections.summary: The Jobs Support Scheme is enhanced to 75% wage offset for hotels, travel agencies, attractions, cruise operators and MICE venues, plus $90 million for tourism.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: As mentioned earlier, I will therefore also enhance the Jobs Support Scheme for licensed hotels, travel agencies, tourist attractions, cruise terminals and operators, and purpose-built MICE venue operators, to offset a total of 75% of the first $4,600 of monthly wages.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: In addition, I will set aside $90 million to help the tourism industry rebound strongly, when the time is right.

sections.label: Support for F&B firms
sections.summary: The Jobs Support Scheme for F&B firms is enhanced to 50% wage offset, and the Point-to-Point Support Package is extended and enhanced at a cost of $95 million.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: As mentioned earlier, I will enhance the Jobs Support Scheme for F&B firms by providing a total of 50% wage offset, for the first $4,600 of monthly wages.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: To support them, we will extend and enhance the Point-to-Point Support Package.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: This will cost the Government another $95 million.

sections.label: Budget for emerging stronger
sections.summary: $1.9 billion is set aside in this Budget so Singapore can emerge stronger as an economy and society.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: If we prepare ourselves well today, we can emerge stronger, not only as an economy, but as a society.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: I will set aside $1.9 billion in this Budget to support this.

sections.label: Training support scheme enhancements
sections.summary: Enhanced training subsidies and absentee payroll are extended to more sectors and all employers, with courses starting before 1 January 2021 covered.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The enhancements to these three schemes will last until December 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: In our Unity Budget, we raised course fee subsidies and absentee payroll to 90% for the aviation, tourism, food services and retail trade sectors, to last until June 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: I will extend the enhanced training support to the arts and culture and land transport sectors, starting from 1 April 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: And I will extend the 90% absentee payroll rates to all employers, to provide additional cash flow relief when they send their workers for training, from 1 May 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The duration of the enhancements will also be extended to cover eligible courses starting before 1 January 2021.

sections.label: Past Reserves draw history
sections.summary: The Government has drawn on Past Reserves only once, during the Global Financial Crisis, when the President approved a $4.9 billion draw.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Until now, the Government has drawn on Past Reserves only once, during the Global Financial Crisis, when the President approved a draw of $4.9 billion to fund the Jobs Credit Scheme and special risk-sharing initiative.

sections.label: Guarantee not triggered
sections.summary: The guarantee was not triggered and there was no draw on the Past Reserves.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: As it turned out, the guarantee was not triggered, and there was no draw on the Past Reserves.

sections.label: President's support for $17 billion draw
sections.summary: The Government has the President's in-principle support to draw up to $17 billion for measures including Jobs Support Scheme enhancements and other schemes.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The Government has obtained the President's in-principle support to draw up to $17 billion to fund some of the measures to save jobs and the economy.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: These include the Jobs Support Scheme enhancements, the Self-Employed Person Income Relief Scheme, the Temporary Bridging Loan Programme, the enhanced Enterprise Financing Scheme and the enhanced Aviation Support Package.

sections.label: FY2020 budget deficit raised
sections.summary: The announced measures raise the Overall Budget Deficit for FY2020 to $39.2 billion, which remains fiscally sustainable through disciplined use of Past Reserves.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The measures that I have announced today will raise the Overall Budget Deficit for FY2020 to $39.2 billion.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We are able to support this unprecedented deficit and still remain fiscally sustainable because we have been disciplined in the use of Past Reserves, tapping on it only in exceptional circumstances like this.

sections.label: $55 billion budget for jobs
sections.summary: A $55 billion budget aims to save jobs and help enterprises, extending the Jobs Support Scheme and introducing a $1.2 billion Self-Employed Persons Income Relief Scheme.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: To help Singaporeans tide over this difficult period, we have drawn up a $55 billion budget aimed at saving jobs, help enterprises and securing our future.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: First, our immediate task is to save jobs and protect Singaporeans' livelihood.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Hence, we have extended the Jobs Support Scheme by six months.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We will also raise the Government's co-funding of wages from 8% to 25%.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: This is to prevent companies from retrenching local workers due to a lack of funds.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We will introduce a $1.2-billlion dollar Self-Employed Persons Income Relief Scheme.

sections.label: Reserves use in-principle support
sections.summary: The government has in-principal support from President Halimah Yacob to draw on reserves to fund measures.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The government has obtained in-principal support from President Halimah Yacob to draw on our reserves to fund the series of measures.

sections.label: President Speaker Deputy Speakers pay cut
sections.summary: The President, Speaker and both Deputy Speakers will take a similar three-month pay cut in total.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The President, Speaker and both Deputy Speakers have informed me that they will join in and take a similar three-month pay cut in total.

sections.label: Vigilance and standing with Singaporeans
sections.summary: Singapore must stay vigilant, decide on facts, plan long term, and stand with Singaporeans and frontline workers.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We must continue to be on high vigilance, mentally and psychologically prepared for every scenario.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We will do our best to anticipate and respond to developments, make decisions based on facts and evidence, and exercise judgement when there are trade-offs.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: While we attend to the immediate and urgent tasks, we will set our sights on the long term so that Singapore comes out of this crisis stronger as a nation.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: And we will stand with Singaporeans from all walks of life to battle this crisis together.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We will stand with our dedicated and courageous frontline workers – healthcare workers, cleaning staff, immigration officers, public transport workers – who keep Singapore going, despite the risks they face on the job.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We will stand with our workers and businesses to ride through this economic storm together and overcome this challenge to our growth and prosperity.

sections.label: Global infections and Singapore measures
sections.summary: Over one million people worldwide are infected; Singapore stepped up measures, latest a one-month circuit breaker.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: More than one million people around the world have now been infected with the virus.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In Singapore, we have progressively stepped up measures – restricting travels, raised to DORSCON Orange, working from home, safety distancing and others – the latest being the stepped-up measures to apply a one-month circuit breaker to quell the recent sharp rises in cases.

sections.label: MTI GDP forecast downgrade
sections.summary: The latest MTI forecast downgraded Singapore's GDP growth to -4% to -1%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The latest MTI forecast downgraded Singapore's GDP growth to -4% to -1%.

sections.label: Job Support Scheme expansion
sections.summary: The Job Support Scheme was expanded to cover 75% of all workers for the first $4,600 of monthly salary.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Of course, the key focus must be still to save livelihoods and to support businesses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: I am very glad that the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance has further expanded the Job Support Scheme to cover 75% of all workers in Singapore for the first $4,600 of their monthly salary and the payout will be made in April – as soon as next week, if they have PayNow and Giro.

sections.label: COVID-19 Support Grant and Temporary Relief Fund
sections.summary: The COVID-19 Support Grant gives $800 a month for three months to lower and middle income Singaporeans who lost jobs, with Temporary Relief Fund for April.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: To help those who lost their jobs or have seen significant drops in income due to COVID-19, the COVID-19 Support Grant (CSG) is introduced.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The CSG provides cash grant of $800 a month for three months for lower and middle income Singaporeans who lost their jobs due to the virus.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: As the scheme can only be ready for application from May 2020 onwards, those who need immediate assistance in April can apply for the Temporary Relief Fund (TRF).

sections.label: Community Centre TRF applications and SGUnited Jobs
sections.summary: Over 1,500 TRF applications came to one Community Centre in a week, and 10,000 public sector jobs are committed under SGUnited Jobs Initiative.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Just at my Community Centre alone, we have received more than 1,500 TRF applications in the last one week.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Many of residents have been badly impacted by the crisis in the last two months and are in need of immediate relief.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Therefore, the visible hand of the Government or G will have to come in again, and I am glad we are committing to creating 10,000 jobs, primarily in the public sector over the next one year under the SGUnited Jobs Initiative.

sections.label: $20 billion loan capital for companies
sections.summary: $20 billion in loan capital is set aside to catalyse private sector loan capital for promising companies with strong capabilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Of significance is also the $20 billion loan capital set aside to catalyse the private sector loan capital to support promising companies with strong capabilities.

sections.label: Resilience and Solidarity Budgets and Job Support Scheme
sections.summary: The Resilience and Solidarity Budgets focus on health, safety and livelihoods, with $15.1 billion for the Job Support Scheme paying 25% of monthly wages.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: The Supplementary or Resilience Budget and now the Solidarity Budget are much needed as the individual lives, families, communities and businesses are hurting.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: The primary focus of the Resilience Budget and the Solidarity Budget is the health and safety of every Singaporean and protecting livelihoods, supporting viable businesses, manage the immediate challenges of cash flow, cost and credit given the drastic and sudden impact on business demand and supply.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: The $15.1 billion which Deputy Prime Minister Heng had outlined out of the $48 billion Resilience Budget for the Job Support Scheme (JSS) and now with the additional enhanced Job Support Scheme with the Solidarity Budget will pay 25% of monthly wages for every Singaporean worker in employment, capped at an income level of $4,600, for nine months until the end of 2020.

sections.label: Temporary Relief Fund and COVID-Support Grant income support
sections.summary: The Temporary Relief Fund and COVID-Support Grant provide three months of partial income support for those with impacted income or lost jobs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: The Temporary Relief Fund as well as the COVID-Support Grant which provide three months of partial income support would go some way to help those whose income has been impacted or jobs have been lost.

sections.label: SIRS and CSG means testing flexibility
sections.summary: Means testing is necessary for SIRS and CSG eligibility, but the speaker hopes for flexibility for self-employed persons needing help to qualify.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: For the Self-Employed Persons Income Relief Scheme (SIRS) and the COVID-19 Support Grant (CSG), while means testing is necessary for their eligibility, I do hope that even with the enhanced eligibility criteria so-called the increase of the annual value of eligibility criteria for the household type, I do hope that there will still be flexibility in cases where self-employed persons do need help in qualifying for this support.

sections.label: Briefing volunteers on mask distribution
sections.summary: The speaker briefed almost 70 volunteers digitally to distribute re-usable masks over the weekend while avoiding large group meetings.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Just last weekend, while we had to avoid large group meetings to prevent the possible spread of COVID-19, I was glad that I was still able to brief almost 70 of our volunteers at the same time, using digital technology to be able to ensure that we were able to distribute the re-usable masks over the weekend.

sections.label: Singapore's 30% nutritional needs target
sections.summary: Singapore aims to produce 30% of its nutritional needs by 2030, requiring research, land, and mobilised local talent.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Many Singaporeans are now aware of and appreciate the importance of Singapore’s target of producing 30% of Singapore’s nutritional needs by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Beyond investing in research and technology to achieve productivity in farming and unlocking physical land for farming, we must also mobilise Singaporeans, both young and old, to develop our local talent to understand urban food production processes and business models to accelerate our efforts to achieve our ambitious target.

sections.label: Working together against COVID-19
sections.summary: Beyond the Resilience and Solidarity Budgets, individuals, businesses and the Government must work together against COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: What is clear is that beyond the Resilience and Solidarity Budgets which are much needed, it will take each and every one of us, as well as businesses and the Government to work together in this fight against COVID-19.

sections.label: Supplementary Budget drawing on reserves
sections.summary: The House debates a supplementary Budget drawing on reserves about a month after approving the annual Budget and Solidarity Budget.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To that end, it is mind-boggling that this House is debating a supplementary Budget that draws on the reserves just about one month after we have approved the annual Budget which included a first package of COVID-19 support measures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It was a Budget which Deputy Prime Minister Heng, with some pride announced, did not draw down past reserves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: And since then, yet another package of measures in the shape of the Solidarity Budget has also been introduced.

sections.label: Support for impacted industries and self-employed
sections.summary: Heavily impacted industries receive higher Jobs Support Scheme co-funding until end-2020, and self-employed Singaporeans receive nine months of assistance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For example, heavily impacted industries crucial for our open economy receive higher co-funding under the Jobs Support Scheme until the end of 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Self-employed Singaporeans, who are amongst the worst impacted by this crisis, receive nine months of assistance.

sections.label: Resilience Budget schemes and new normal
sections.summary: The Resilience Budget provides temporary taxpayer-funded unemployment insurance, income support, food vouchers and self-employed protection, prompting a question about a new normal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Through the Resilience Budget, we now have a taxpayer-funded unemployment insurance, income support for lower income families, food vouchers for the poor, and protection for the self-employed – albeit temporary.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Given the long-term effects of the COVID-19 pandemic on our economy and society, will these schemes represent a new normal, akin to a multi-year New Deal to help Singaporeans cope and bounce back from economic hardship?

sections.label: Acting decisively, drawing on reserves
sections.summary: The speaker says acting decisively is needed to avoid damage to national unity, and supports drawing on reserves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: And unless we act decisively in the days, months and years ahead, this stain will not go away and it will eat at our collective conscience, damaging our sense of national unity and solidarity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: We are nearing the end of the term of Government, and the accumulated surpluses have come in handy to meet public needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Even so, we are now needing to draw on the reserves, and I support this.

sections.label: Reserves in first year
sections.summary: The speaker says a government drawing on reserves in its first year is unprecedented but may happen.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: A government drawing on the reserves in its first year of the new term is unprecedented, but this may be the case if we are looking at additional support in the coming months.

sections.label: Temporarily ceasing CPF contributions
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Government to consider temporarily stopping employer and employee CPF contributions for three to six months.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Yes, I am not asking us to dip into our CPF, but I would like to ask the Government to consider whether is it possible to temporarily cease both employer and employee CPF contributions.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: To reduce the manpower cost of the employers and to increase the monthly take home pay of our salaried workers, can we temporarily stop CPF contributions for the next three to six months?

sections.label: Deferring HDB mortgage repayments
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether HDB can defer all mortgage repayments for three to six months, interest free.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Just like the recent announcements for deferment of housing loans under MAS and the banks, and the announcement in the Budget regarding deferment of study loans repayments, can HDB consider deferring all HDB mortgages repayment for the next three to six months?

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In addition, I hope this deferment can be interest free so that HDB mortgagees loans repayment period need not be lengthened too much.

sections.label: Bringing forward S&CC rebates
sections.summary: The speaker suggests bringing forward S&CC and U Save rebates to the next three months.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: To further ease the households expenses, Government has announced 1.5 to 3.5 months of S&CC rebates and U Save in Budget 2020.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I would suggest these rebates be brought forward to the next three months instead of spacing out throughout the year.

sections.label: Proving Lee Kuan Yew right
sections.summary: The speaker cites Lee Kuan Yew on Singaporeans' physical and spiritual ruggedness and says this is the time to prove him right.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Our founding Prime Minister Lee Kuan Yew had once spoken about Singaporeans as people with physical and spiritual ruggedness.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: This is the time that we prove him right.

sections.label: Taxi drivers grocery deliveries
sections.summary: Minister Khaw Boon Wan announced taxi and private-hire drivers can help make grocery and food deliveries, with 10,000 taxis and 25,000 cabbies facing falling income.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Minister Khaw Boon Wan recently announced that taxi and private-hire car drivers can now help to make grocery and food deliveries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: As the taxi Head, I am all for the idea.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: We have 10,000 taxis and 25,000 cabbies who are experiencing a deep drop in their income from the lack of passengers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Cabbies' income will continue to drop even we have waived their taxi rental completely for the next 28 days.

sections.label: Waiving parking charges for deliveries
sections.summary: The speaker appeals to HDB to waive parking charges for delivery vehicles during this period.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: The issue of parking is quite small still as compared to other issues, but I would still like to appeal to HDB to waive the parking charges for delivery vehicles in this trying period.

sections.label: MOM allows workers other jobs
sections.summary: MOM has allowed workers in sectors badly affected by COVID-19 to take on other jobs while on paid or unpaid leave.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Can they be given the opportunity to step up and earn some money?

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: We understand that MOM has already allowed workers, especially those employed in sectors which are badly affected by the COVID-19 outbreak, to take on other jobs while they are on paid leave or unpaid leave, including airport ground handling staff, hotel chambermaid, waiter and waitress and so on.

sections.label: Investing in homegrown food
sections.summary: The speaker says it would be wise to invest in homegrown food and encourage urban farming and farm plots around office buildings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: While we have always diversified our food supplies, to obtain food from as many countries as possible, but COVID-19 is affecting every country.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: And while I hope another COVID-19 will not happen for the next century, it would be wise for us to think of how to invest in homegrown food.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: We could encourage the growth of urban farming, the creation of farm plots around office buildings which staff can use to grow vegetables for not just for own consumption, but also for the mental well-being.

sections.label: Hawkers online sales cashless transactions
sections.summary: After 7 April hawkers must learn online platforms to sell food, and cashless transactions must be popularised.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Similarly, our hawkers are not used to selling food online.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: But after 7 April, they must learn to use online platforms to sell food to make up for the loss of no dining-in.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Before, people like to use cash in the form of notes and coins that are good conduits for bacteria.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Therefore, we have to popularise cashless transactions as much as possible.

sections.label: Whole-of-nation effort against COVID-19
sections.summary: The speaker states that in the long battle against COVID-19, a whole-of-nation effort matters, not just a whole-of-Government effort.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: (In English): In the long battle against COVID-19, it is not just a whole-of-Government effort that matter; it is a whole-of-nation effort.

sections.label: Budget packages and GDP share
sections.summary: The Resilience Budget costs $48 billion, and with earlier packages totals about 11% of GDP, rising to about 12% with the Solidarity Budget.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Resilience Budget before this House had a price tag of $48 billion.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Together with the first package announced in the Unity Budget in February, the total of about $55 billion amounts to about 11% of our GDP.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This is within the GDP range of the packages previously announced by some other governments.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I also note the further support measures just announced in the Solidarity Budget, which bring the total package to about 12% of GDP.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: As mentioned by Workers' Party Secretary-General Mr Pritam Singh earlier, we will vote in support of the proposed Government measures.

sections.label: Temporary Relief Fund and Support Grant
sections.summary: The Temporary Relief Fund pays a one-time $500 in April and the COVID-19 Support Grant gives $800 monthly for three months, with questions on proving COVID-19 caused job loss.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Temporary Relief Fund has been announced to be a one-time $500 cash payout in the month of April while the COVID-19 Support Grant gives three months of support at $800 per month for three months.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The intention behind these measures is to put cash into the hands of households where jobs have disappeared, and I agree with that.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It is stated that to qualify for the payments, the job loss must be due to COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Does the applicant have to prove the causal connection between COVID-19 and the job loss?

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: If he is terminated by the company now, will his application for assistance be rejected because it is arguable that his job loss was not caused by the virus outbreak?

sections.label: Tentage contractor and Jobs Support Scheme
sections.summary: A tentage contractor folded as temple dinners stopped, and the speaker supports the measures while seeking clarification on the Jobs Support Scheme.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For instance, we know of a tentage contractor who has recently had to fold as there have been no temple dinners for months.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: We will support the Government's proposed measures and I look forward to the Government's clarifications on the queries I have raised about the Jobs Support Scheme and the measures to assist displaced workers.

sections.label: Two Supplementary Budgets protecting people
sections.summary: The Government rolled out the Resilience Budget and Solidarity Budget, whose central theme is protecting people financially devastated by the crisis.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: The Government has rolled out two unprecedented Supplementary Budgets – the Resilience Budget and the Solidarity Budget.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: The central theme running through these two Budgets is the need to protect our people, people who have been financially devastated by this crisis.

sections.label: Government as buyer and seller of last resort
sections.summary: The speaker states that only the Government can act as the buyer and seller of last resort for goods and services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: In my mind, there is only one entity that can act as the buyer and seller of last resort for goods and services, and that is the Government.

sections.label: Sustained investment in infrastructure and industries
sections.summary: As seller of last resort, the Government must keep investing in infrastructure and strategic industries like health, water, food, electricity, masks and defence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: As a seller of last resort, the Government needs to continue to make sustained investment in our infrastructure and strategic industries, especially in public utilities and essential services – health, water, food, electricity, masks and even weapons for our national defence – because this pandemic has shown that our survival is too important to be left to the invisible hand of the market.

sections.label: World's first contact tracing app
sections.summary: Engineers created TraceTogether, described as the world's first contact tracing app.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Our engineers have put together the world's first contact tracing app, TraceTogether.

sections.label: Pride in Singapore's COVID response
sections.summary: The speaker praises the Government, leaders, public servants, frontline workers and Singaporeans for mobilising society.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: The way that the Government has pulled out all the stops and mobilised society in such a way that makes me proud to call myself a Singaporean.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I am proud of our Prime Minister, our Deputy Prime Minister, our Ministers, our public servants, our frontline workers and all manners of Singaporeans who have stepped up to be counted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: We need leadership at this critical juncture and I am proud to say that our Government has unequivocally provided this.

sections.label: Elected leaders mean life and death
sections.summary: The passage states that the leaders we elect can mean life and death for our people.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: The leaders that we elect can mean life and death for our people.

sections.label: Urging Singaporeans to join fight
sections.summary: The speaker calls serving the nation a privilege and urges all Singaporeans to join the fight.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: It is, indeed, a privilege and an honour to be of service to one's nation and one's people.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I urge all Singaporeans to come forward and join the fight of our lifetime.

sections.label: Budget and Resilience Budget measures
sections.summary: A $6.4 billion Budget provision and a further Resilience Budget on 26 March 2020 addressed COVID-19 measures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The Budget provided for what seemed to be a very generous provision of $6.4 billion to deal with the impact of COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: There was a surge of cases all around the world and the second wave of COVID-19 became very real as the numbers of locally transmitted cases began to rise.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: This led to additional restrictive measures being implemented to prevent the spread and a further Resilience Budget being announced on 26 March 2020 to help mitigate the impact of these further measures.

sections.label: 120 new cases yesterday
sections.summary: The passage states there were 120 new cases the previous day, mostly locally transmitted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Just yesterday, there were a 120 new cases, the majority being locally transmitted.

sections.label: Circuit breaker as last chance
sections.summary: The circuit breaker is described as the last chance to prevent going where many other countries have gone.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The circuit breaker is our last chance to prevent going where many other countries have gone.

sections.label: Cost of circuit breaker measures
sections.summary: The measures cost just under $6 billion, a further addition to the Budget, as the price of one month of circuit breaker mode.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: But it also tells us the steep price we have to pay for these measures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: It is just under $6 billion and a further addition to the Budget and this is the price we pay for going on circuit breaker mode for one month.

sections.label: Brown rice given during DORSCON Orange
sections.summary: When DORSCON Orange was announced and many places ran out of rice, he carried on an initiative giving out about 2,000 kg of brown rice to those who needed it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: At that time when DORSCON Orange was announced and many places were running out of rice, he carried on with an initiative to give out about 2,000 kg of brown rice to those who needed it.

sections.label: Support for employers and workers
sections.summary: Employers were concerned about wages, and substantial support is coming, particularly for the large base of workers, to cushion the financial and economic impact.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Employers were concerned about wages to be paid to their workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: There is going to be substantial support for that, particularly for the large base of workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: There is going to be support for that as well.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: So, the main aim of the Government is to cushion the financial and economic impact in the next month for a very large part of the country.

sections.label: Outbreak in workers' dormitories
sections.summary: The latest outbreak has taken place in workers' dormitories and some 20,000 workers have now been quarantined.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: You will also realise that the latest outbreak has taken place in workers’ dormitories and some 20,000 workers have now been quarantined.

sections.label: Possible move to total lockdown
sections.summary: If it gets worse and the spread becomes widespread, the country may have no choice but to move towards a total lockdown like many other countries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: On the other hand, if it gets worse, our country may have no choice but to move towards a total lockdown like many other countries have if the spread of the disease becomes widespread.

sections.label: Stimulus package and Solidarity Budget
sections.summary: Measures announced on 26 March 2020 were expected to be about $48 billion, more than three times earlier estimates, followed by a Solidarity Budget.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Before Deputy Prime Minister Heng's announcement on 26 March 2020, I recall The Straits Times carrying an article on 22 March 2020, with the prediction of several financial institutions that the stimulus package "might be in the region of $15 billion".

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: That the measures announced by Deputy Prime Minister Heng on 26 March 2020 were expected to be more than three times that estimate at about $48 billion, have left many in no doubt that this Government is prepared to stand together with its citizens in times of difficulty, especially with today's Solidarity Budget of even more enhanced support measures.

sections.label: Supplementary Budget business support measures
sections.summary: The Supplementary Budget expands tax and wage support for businesses, and the manufacturing sector benefits from these cross-cutting measures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Supplementary Budget expands and deepens a wide range of instruments to provide support for businesses, with a focus on tax and wage support to assist with these three Cs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Although there were no specific measures for the manufacturing sector, the support measures cut across all businesses and the manufacturing sector will, therefore, benefit from the same.

sections.label: Guarantor age issue for loans
sections.summary: Members report financial institutions turned them away because they could not find shareholders below 60 years old to act as guarantors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Thirdly, while our members appreciate the measures in improving the working capital loans, our members have also provided feedback that financial institutions have turned them away as they have been unable to find shareholders who are below 60 years old to act as guarantors.

sections.label: SMEs Go Digital and grants
sections.summary: The Supplementary Budget expands the SMEs Go Digital programme and support under the Enterprise Development Grant and Productivity Solutions Grant.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Supplementary Budget includes the expanding of the SMEs Go Digital – Digital Project Management Services programme to include more solutions for business continuity and expanded support under the Enterprise Development Grant and Productivity Solutions Grant.

sections.label: Tapping into national reserves
sections.summary: The Government has taken the extraordinary move in this Supplementary Budget to tap into our reserves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Government has taken the extraordinary move in this Supplementary Budget to tap into our reserves.

sections.label: Reciprocal employer and employee commitment
sections.summary: Businesses should strive to retain jobs and plan for rebound, while employees and unions should remember employers' sacrifices, with tripartite relations used to pass on relief measures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In this spirit of reciprocity of good intent and measures, it is only right that a reciprocal commitment is required on the part of businesses to strive to retain as many jobs as possible, plan ahead for the economic rebound and ensure that this drawdown from the reserves, accumulated over decades of a sound and prudent financial policy, are well accounted for by this generation of Singaporeans to the next.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Employers not only have to deal with the numerous ongoing demands of the business, take care of employee welfare and livelihood, but employers, too, have families and dependants to account to.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I would, therefore, like to sound a call to employees and to worker unions that when COVID-19 blows over and this dust has settled, do not forget the employer that has fought hard and made sacrifices for you to keep your job or the employer that has sent you for training to increase your knowledge and keep you updated in the evolving workforce.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Quite apart from the rigidity of laws and regulations, the existing relations within the tripartite partnership can be utilised to prod and cajole employers to pass on relief measures to employees, especially with the critical aim of retaining jobs and upskilling the workforce.

sections.label: Tripartite partnership and penal deterrence
sections.summary: The speaker says law and penalties are still required but greater tripartite engagement can complement legal provisions and reduce the need for penal deterrence, and supports the Supplementary Budget Statement 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For clarity, I am not saying that the use of law and penalties is not required but there should be greater engagement through the tripartite partnership which can run complementary to legal provisions and reduce the necessity of the use of penal deterrence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I firmly support the Supplementary Budget Statement 2020.

sections.label: Airport Development Levy waiver
sections.summary: The Government will waive the Airport Development Levy until the end of March next year.

sentences.speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: The Government will also waive the Airport Development Levy (ADL) until the end of March next year.

sections.label: Suspending Terminal 2 operations
sections.summary: Operations at Terminal 2 will be suspended for 18 months from 1 May next month, saving running costs and speeding up upgrading works by up to one year.

sentences.speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: After much deliberation, we have decided to suspend operations at Terminal 2 (T2) for 18 months from 1 May next month.

sentences.speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: We will save on running costs for the airport operator, retail tenants, airlines and ground handlers.

sentences.speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: Importantly, it also allows us to speed up the current upgrading works at T2 and shorten the project time by up to one year.

sections.label: Aviation staff volunteering as care ambassadors
sections.summary: About 800 crew and ground staff from aviation companies including SIA have come forward to help at hospitals, Social Service Offices and NTUC.

sentences.speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: To-date, about 800 crew and ground staff from our aviation companies including SIA have come forward to help out at our hospitals as care ambassadors, at Social Service Offices (SSOs) to help process applications for social support and at NTUC as customer service associates.

sections.label: ComfortDelGro support for transport schemes
sections.summary: ComfortDelGro's suggestions helped shape the Point-to-Point Support Package and it contributed more than its share and chipped in for the Transport Ambassador scheme.

sentences.speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: His many suggestions to me helped us shape the Point-to-Point Support Package and ComfortDelGro contributed more than its share.

sentences.speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: When we suggested the Transport Ambassador scheme to help taxi drivers earn extra allowance, ComfortDelGro chipped in readily.

sections.label: Suspension of ERP and COE
sections.summary: The Minister for Transport having to suspend ERP, COE and discourage public transport use shows the situation is serious.

sentences.speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: When the Minister for Transport has to suspend ERP, COE and discourage the use of public transport, you know the situation is serious.

sections.label: Sea port kept open
sections.summary: Singapore kept its sea port open throughout the crisis and is committed to keeping it open.

sentences.speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: Unlike others, we kept our sea port open throughout this crisis and we are committed to keeping it open.

sections.label: Land link with Johor
sections.summary: Through bilateral cooperation, the land link with Johor stays open for essential goods despite the Movement Control Order.

sentences.speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: Nearer home, with bilateral cooperation, our land link with Johor remains open for essential goods despite the Movement Control Order (MCO).

sections.label: Singaporeans overcoming crisis together
sections.summary: Over 42 years in Government service, the speaker has seen Singaporeans come together to overcome crises, and expects 2020 to be remembered as their finest moment.

sentences.speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: Over my 42 years in Government service, I have seen how Singaporeans came together to confront and overcome a crisis.

sentences.speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Infrastructure and Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: Many years from now, I am sure our children and our grandchildren will look back at 2020 as our finest moment – when Singaporeans will again come together to defeat COVID-19 and emerge stronger.

sections.label: Cost of shutting non-essential services
sections.summary: Analysts estimate a month-long shutdown of non-essential services could cost about $5 to $10 billion, or 2% of GDP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Some analysts and economists estimate the shutting down of non-essential services for a month could cost from about $5 to $10 billion or 2% of GDP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Non-essential services cover roughly about 30% of GDP, including a large proportion of sectors such as retail, gaming, construction of residential and office projects, hospitality and business services.

sections.label: Workers in cold storage
sections.summary: Because sectors like retail, F&B and construction are labour-intensive, roughly 1.3 million workers may be in cold storage for a month.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: This is because many of the sectors such as retail, F&B and construction are more labour-intensive than essential services such as financial services or electronics manufacturing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: So, roughly 1.3 million workers may be in cold storage for a month albeit productive, possibly, out of the 3.78 million employed at end of 2019.

sections.label: Rental waivers increased
sections.summary: The impact of the Enhanced Property Tax Rebate is small relative to the JSS, and total rental waivers have been increased to $334 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The impact of the Enhanced Property Tax Rebate is quite small relative to the JSS and then landlords may not pass the savings to retail tenants.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I am glad that the total amount of rental waivers has been increased to $334 million to tide over eligible properties for three months.

sections.label: Work permit rebate
sections.summary: Firms receive a $650 rebate for each work permit or S Pass holder.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Firms do get a rebate of $650 for each of the work permit or S Pass holders.

sections.label: Enhanced Temporary Bridging Loan programme
sections.summary: The Government will shoulder 80% of default risk and 90% re-sharing until March 2021 under the Enhanced Temporary Bridging Loan programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Under the Enhanced Temporary Bridging Loan programme, the Government will shoulder 80% of default risk and now 90% re-sharing until March 2021.

sections.label: Pawnshop loans and macro-prudential measures
sections.summary: Outstanding pawnshop loans rose 3.4% in Q4 2019, and the speaker urges reviewing TDSR and LTV limits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Yet outstanding pawnshop loans have picked up by 3.4% in the fourth quarter of 2019, the fastest pace since the year before in 2018.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Even though interest rates have fallen, access to bank credit remains tight because of TDSR and prudential measures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: So, I urge the Government to conduct a further review on the macro-prudential measures and consider easing on macro-prudential measures in totality, especially the Total Debt Servicing Ratio (TDSR) and Loan-to-Value (LTV) limits.

sections.label: CPF employer contribution question
sections.summary: A resident asked whether CPF contribution requirement from employers has been reduced.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Recently, a resident asked me if it is true that CPF contribution requirement from employers has been reduced.

sections.label: Food resilience and social pressures
sections.summary: The passage asks about producing 50% of nutritional needs by 2030 and notes food supply and social pressures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: And we are strengthening our food resilience for the long term.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: But instead of a 30 by 30 vision, can we aim to produce 50% or more of our nutritional needs by 2030, up from less than 10% today?

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: While the supply of food is functioning well in most countries and Singapore at present, problems could start to be seen within weeks and intensify over the following two months as key fruits and vegetables come into season.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: These types of produce often have short ripening times and are highly perishable and need skilled pickers to work quickly and at the right time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: In addition, as governments impose lockdowns in countries across the world, recruiting seasonal workers will become impossible unless measures are taken to ensure vital workers can still move around, while preventing the virus from spreading.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Charities have reported receiving less donations, as in times of an impending economic crisis, people have understandably tightened their purse strings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Social workers too will be overwhelmed with the new schemes and with more people seeking help in these times.

sections.label: Appreciation for government help
sections.summary: People appreciate the Singapore Government and Singaporeans, including the enhanced Job Support Scheme of up to 75% subsidy.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: But all of them tell me that while things are difficult, they appreciate what the Singapore Government and Singaporeans are doing together.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: And I am sure many will also appreciate the extra help that Deputy Prime Minister announced today, on top of the two Budgets, especially the enhanced Job Support Scheme of up to 75% subsidy.

sections.label: SIRS criteria and Annual Value
sections.summary: Some do not meet SIRS criteria, and the speaker welcomes broadening criteria by raising Annual Value from $13,000 to $21,000.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: Because they do not meet the criteria for SIRS.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: So, again, I am happy to hear a broadening of criteria for these people where the Annual Value (AV) is raised from $13,000 to $21,000.

sections.label: NTUC facilitating appeals for freelancers
sections.summary: NTUC and the Labour Movement will work to facilitate appeals starting no later than 20 April for freelancers and self-employed facing hard times.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: We will try our very best to push for inclusion and make this process as straightforward as possible.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: I know that many freelancers and self-employed are going through hard times and as such, we, in NTUC and the Labour Movement will work to facilitate appeals starting no later than 20 April.

sections.label: Small amount but counts
sections.summary: The amount is $200-$300, which is not large, but every little bit counts.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: While this is not a large amount, $200-$300, but every little bit counts.

sections.label: SIA cabin crew redeployed
sections.summary: Cabin crew from SIA are being trained and redeployed as SG Care and Safe Distancing Ambassadors.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: For example, as Minister Khaw has also mentioned, cabin crew from SIA are being trained and redeployed for meaningful work as SG Care and Safe Distancing Ambassadors.

sections.label: Tripartite partners' shared objectives
sections.summary: The tripartite partners share the same objectives: sustain companies, sustain jobs and secure the future.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: Our objectives across the tripartite partners are the same: sustain our companies; sustaining our jobs and securing our future.

sections.label: NTUC appeals for SIRS-ineligible self-employed
sections.summary: From 20 April, NTUC will help self-employed persons not eligible for SIRS appeal to the Government to benefit from the scheme.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: Some of them are not eligible for the Self-Employed Person Income Relief Scheme (SIRS).

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: From 20 April, NTUC will help the self-employed persons who are not eligible for SIRS to appeal to the Government so that they can benefit from this scheme as well.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: Both NTUC and the Government share the same goal – the support packages must sustain our companies, sustain our jobs and secure our future.

sections.label: Warehouses full assurance
sections.summary: The Government, Labour Movement and employers work with Singaporeans, and warehouses are quite full.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: The Government, the Labour Movement and employers are working with Singaporeans, to overcome this together.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: First, I would like to assure everyone in the House and Singaporeans outside, that our warehouses are quite full.

sections.label: Fairprice Housebrand price freeze
sections.summary: In March 2019, prices of the top 100 Fairprice Housebrand essential products were frozen for 15 months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: In March last year, 2019, we had announced we would freeze the prices of the top 100 Fairprice Housebrand essential products for 15 months regardless of changes in supply and external factors.

sections.label: Jobs and people served
sections.summary: The group provides jobs to over 21,000 people and serves over two million people daily.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: As a group, we provide jobs to over 21,000 people and we serve over two million people everyday.

sections.label: Singapore 30/30 food vision
sections.summary: Singapore aims to have 30% of food consumption from local sources by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Singapore has a 30/30 vision – to have 30% of our food consumption coming from local sources by year 2030.

sections.label: Workforce over 50 years old
sections.summary: More than 50% of the workforce is more than 50 years old.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: More than 50% of our workforce is more than 50 years old.

sections.label: Resilience and Solidarity Budget reserves
sections.summary: The $53 billion Supplementary Resilience and Solidarity Budget is financed by reserves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: The Supplementary Resilience and Solidarity Budget at $53 billion is an enormous package to help individuals, families and businesses alike.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: People know this but what makes it really extraordinary is that it is financed by our reserves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: How can a small country with no oil, nothing valuable to sell, accumulate these reserves?

sections.label: Support for Resilience and Solidarity Budgets
sections.summary: A speaker supports the Resilience and Solidarity Budgets on behalf of NTUC, NTUC Enterprise, NTUC FairPrice Group and residents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Unity, resilience, solidarity and most of all, a shared history and a shared future.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: So, on behalf of all of us at NTUC, NTUC Enterprise and NTUC FairPrice Group, as well as my residents at Braddell Heights and Marine Parade GRC, I am happy and I am very proud to support the Resilience and Solidarity Budgets.

sections.label: Sitting suspended, reserves use
sections.summary: The Sitting is suspended until 5.30 pm, and the Speaker is heartened by the decisive use of reserves for the Budgets.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Anyway, so I thought we will take a break now.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: I suspend the Sitting and will take the Chair at 5.30 pm.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Sitting accordingly suspended  at 5.10 pm until 5.30 pm.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I am also heartened to see the decisive use of our reserves to deliver on the Resilience and Solidarity Budgets.

sections.label: Resilience Budget temporary jobs
sections.summary: The Resilience Budget created temporary jobs, and more can be considered if the economy worsens, citing 1930s US.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Our Resilience Budget has created some temporary jobs, which is a very solid move.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: But if the economic front continues to deteroriate, we can consider doing more and take a leaf from the US government in the 1930s.

sections.label: Tapping unemployed professionals for transformation
sections.summary: The WPA did not compete with the private sector, so unemployed professionals and management talent could help Ministries streamline, digitise and transform.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The WPA were also beneficiaries to US in the long run and they were not designed or geared to compete with the private sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Therefore, in a similar way, can we explore tapping on the unemployed professionals and management talent to help every Ministry identify processes to streamline, digitise and perhaps, even transform?

sections.label: Business graduates AI diploma
sections.summary: One possibility is getting non-technical, especially business, graduates to do a one-year advanced diploma or minor in AI, data-science and programming.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: One possibility is to get non-technical, especially business graduates, to do a one-year advance diploma or a minor in AI, data-science and programming.

sections.label: Task force led by Senior Ministers
sections.summary: Because sense-making may be too complex, Singapore can consider a task force of 30, perhaps led by both Senior Ministers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: It may be too complex for any individual groups of professionals, experts or policy-makers to sense-make.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Therefore, Singapore can consider creating a task force, a group of 30, perhaps be led by both of our Senior Ministers.

sections.label: Reserves, ASEAN and middle powers
sections.summary: The passage asks how the crisis affects national reserves, the ASEAN growth story, cooperation with middle powers, and the NIRC framework.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: How will that affect the asset allocation and investment strategies of our national reserves?

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: And what happens to the ASEAN growth story, especially if developing countries are not able to cope with COVID-19 and cannot raise debt to deal with the economic fall-out?

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: If multi-lateralism continues to decline, can we form deeper cooperation with capable, trusted and stable middle powers like Australia, Israel, and Japan, to meet long-term challenges on the food, medical and defence fronts?

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: If the world face a prolonged U-shape or L-shape scenario, should we review our NIRC framework and revisit our long-term infrastructure investment plans?

sections.label: Jobs Support Programme discretion
sections.summary: The passage states that quick insights help Singapore stay nimble and hopes the Government considers expanding and giving discretion to the Jobs Support Programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
