sentences.text: Having insights to these questions at the very quickest moments will help Singapore stay nimble amidst unparalleled uncertainty.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I hope the Government can consider expanding and putting some discretion for the Jobs Support Programme.

sections.label: Job support for directors' fees
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Government can consider giving discretionary job support to those whose income is largely limited to directors' fees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Government consider giving job support on a discretionary basis to some of them if their income is largely limited to directors’ fees?

sections.label: Unity Budget frontline support
sections.summary: The passage states that under the Unity Budget, about $800 million was set aside to support frontline agencies fighting and containing the outbreak.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Under the Unity Budget, we put aside about $800 million to support frontline agencies to fight and contain the outbreak.

sections.label: Deficit of $44.3 billion
sections.summary: The passage states that the Deputy Prime Minister said Singapore is in a deficit of $44.3 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Already, we heard from the hon Deputy Prime Minister that we are in a deficit of $44.3 billion.

sections.label: MCO, critical jobs and food imports
sections.summary: The passage describes how Malaysia's MCO caused shortages of lift technicians and prime mover drivers, suggests reviewing Dependency Ratio Ceilings for critical jobs, and notes 90% of food is imported.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In relation to the first point, I learnt anecdotally from my residents that when Malaysia issued the Movement Control Order (MCO) last month, this created a shortage of lift maintenance technicians and prime mover drivers at the ports.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: These are important jobs to ensure that Singapore keeps ticking.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: It may be good to review this and other critical jobs to see whether the Dependency Ratio Ceilings for the relevant sectors need to be adjusted to strengthen the Singaporean Core in these jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: As we all know, 90% of our food is imported.

sections.label: 30 by 30 food target
sections.summary: The 30 by 30 vision is a stretch target because current production is only 10%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The well-known 30 by 30 vision is already a stretch target as our current production level is only 10%.

sections.label: Calamities and agriculture land
sections.summary: Growing natural and man-made calamities affecting global food supply chains may require revisiting the 1% of land set aside for agriculture.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Also, there appears to be more and more natural and man-made calamities affecting global food supply chains nowadays, even putting aside COVID-19 event for the moment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: This may require a revisiting of the setting aside of 1% of our land for agriculture.

sections.label: Temporary Bridging Loan interest costs
sections.summary: A businessman faces about 3.5% annual interest, and the speaker seeks comments on whether enhancing the Temporary Bridging Loan lowers costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: According to him, the current interest is about 3.5% per annum.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: But the bank ultimately may not, with the 3.5%, over and above what he has to pay under the secured loan.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I welcome Deputy Prime Minister's comments on how the enhancing of the Temporary Bridging Loan would have the impact of lowering the costs for businessmen like him.

sections.label: Prime Minister on US-China
sections.summary: The Prime Minister said it will be a very difficult challenge for mankind, with the United States and Chinese swapping insults and blaming each other for the virus.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In a memorable quote, the Prime Minister said and I quote, "Under the best of circumstances, it is going to be a very difficult challenge for mankind, but the United States and Chinese are swapping insults and blaming one another for inventing the virus and letting it loose on the world.

sections.label: Singapore economy 1.9% growth
sections.summary: The Singapore economy grew by 1.9% that year, with job losses far below the 100,000 predicted, though unemployment peaked at about 5%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: No one expected it, but the Singapore economy grew by 1.9% that year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Job losses in Singapore were nowhere near the 100,000 predicted at the start of the year, even though at the peak, unemployment rose to about 5%.

sections.label: Job Support Scheme enhancements
sections.summary: Even as workplaces close temporarily, workers should still put food on the table, so Heng announced further enhancements to the Job Support Scheme.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Even as we close workplaces temporarily, we want to ensure that workers can still put food on the table and meet their financial obligations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: This is why Deputy Prime Minister Heng announced further enhancements to the Job Support Scheme.

sections.label: SIRS Annual Value threshold raised
sections.summary: The SIRS Annual Value threshold rises from $13,000 to $21,000, so about 100,000 SEPs automatically qualify, up from 88,000.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Second, the Annual Value threshold of SIRS will be raised from $13,000 to $21,000.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: With the expanded criteria, about 100,000 SEPs will automatically qualify for SIRS, compared to 88,000 previously.

sections.label: Government-funded traineeship stipend programme
sections.summary: Government funds 80% of trainee stipends and host companies 20%, with up to 8,000 traineeships from 1 June managed by SBF.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Under this programme, the Government will fund 80% of the stipend that each trainee receives, with the host company paying the remaining 20%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: I think that we can imagine in such a time, the stipend may not match the usual starting salaries of graduates but it is still better to have build up some work experience so that the resume has already started building a track record.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: We are looking to support up to 8,000 traineeships this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: It will be rolled out from 1 June with the Singapore Business Federation (SBF) as the programme manager.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: So far, more than 100 companies, such as ST Logistics, Surbana Jurong, Micron, Q&M Dental and Commonwealth Capital, have committed to 1,500 positions.

sections.label: Flat levy rebate per worker
sections.summary: The levy rebate is a flat $750 per worker, based on workers holding work permits and S Passes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: To process the rebate and reach businesses quickly, the levy rebate will be a flat $750 per worker, based on the number of workers holding work permits and S Passes, as employers only pay levies for these workers.

sections.label: Speaker's hopes amid economic hit
sections.summary: The speaker expects things to get tougher, feels hopeful from people's spirit, and says the economy and jobs may take a huge hit.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: In fact, personally, I expect things to get much tougher before they get better.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: I feel hopeful because of the amazing spirit I see in our people – from the ones who make funny videos to cheer us up, there are quite a lot of them, to the ones who rewrite pop hits that go "viral", and also the people who chipped in, do things like make hand sanitisers, sew masks, even though in their entire lives they have never even cooked.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: But now, they experimented with ingredients and certainly, do not like sewing.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: I see businesses that go the extra mile to care for their customers and workers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Likewise, many workers have taken on a lot, a lot more work to help their employers or accepted pay cuts.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Our economy may take a huge hit and so might jobs.

sections.label: ComCare assistance per household
sections.summary: ComCare assistance can only be rendered to one person per household.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: As I understand, the ComCare assistance can only rendered to one per household.

sections.label: ComCare processing time and student aid
sections.summary: ComCare application and approval normally takes about one to one and a half months, and the Government is urged to extend financial assistance to affected Singaporean students.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: As many in this Chamber are aware, the application and approval processes for ComCare assistance normally takes an average of about one to one and a half months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Next, I would like to urge the Government to consider extending the existing financial assistance schemes to Singaporean students whose family incomes are affected by COVID-19.

sections.label: Schools start home-based learning
sections.summary: MOE announced all schools will start home-based learning from 8 April 2020 to 4 May 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: As announced by MOE, all schools will start home-based learning (HBL) from 8 April 2020 to 4 May 2020.

sections.label: MOE loans laptops to students
sections.summary: The speaker acknowledges MOE's recent step of loaning about 3,000 sets of laptops to students.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Having said this, I do acknowledge and note the recent notable steps taken by MOE on loaning about 3,000 sets of laptops to our students.

sections.label: Arts funding during COVID-19
sections.summary: The speaker says the Government will consider the proposals, and notes Singapore's arts and culture sector received more funding amid COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The calls I have made in this speech are not extraordinary calls.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I believe the Government will consider implementing proposals I have put forth as part of our nation's continued efforts to further strengthen our unity and resilience in facing this extraordinary challenging time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In times of crisis, many countries’ arts funding are the first to experience a cut.

sentences.speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, in Singapore, the arts and culture sector received more funding to help improve their skills and ease expenses amid the COVID-19 outbreak.

sections.label: Support for freelance artists
sections.summary: The NAC could consider giving more support to freelance artists and musicians through commissioning new works.

sentences.speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Two, the NAC could consider giving more support for the freelance artists and musicians in the arts community, through commissioning new works, whether arts, music or productions to help weather the storm together, and potentially attract audiences back to theatres and shows.

sections.label: Platform portal Arts.sg
sections.summary: A platform portal Arts.sg would consolidate Singaporean artists' works to share, market and spread awareness of Singapore's arts scene.

sentences.speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Four, to create a platform portal Arts.sg to bring and consolidate all the Singaporean artists’ works on board to share and market to sell spread awareness of Singapore’s arts scene.

sections.label: Additional $55 million for arts
sections.summary: The speaker thanks the Government for setting aside an additional $55 million to the arts and culture sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: (In Mandarin):   	First, I would like to thank the Government for setting aside an additional $55 million to the arts and culture sector.

sections.label: Support for freelance art workers
sections.summary: NAC can consider stepping up efforts and providing support to help freelance art workers access more job opportunities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Second, NAC can consider stepping up efforts and provide support to help freelance art workers access more job opportunities.

sections.label: Reserves funding for support measures
sections.summary: The Deputy Prime Minister said $17 billion from the reserves will fund measures like supporting jobs, helping the self-employed and boosting aviation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: The Deputy Prime Minister had said the $17 billion from the reserves will be used to help fund measures like supporting jobs, helping the self-employed and boosting the hard-hit aviation sector.

sections.label: Ring-fencing reserves and company conditions
sections.summary: The Member asks how the Government will ring-fence reserves money to save jobs, especially in aviation, and whether conditions apply to companies receiving help.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: It must also not be used to protect fat dividends and share buyback schemes for listed companies to appease their shareholders once the crisis blows over.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: Thus, I would like to ask the Minister how is the Government going to ring-fence the money from our reserves to serve this purpose of saving jobs for our workers, especially for those in the aviation industry, since the sector will be receiving the lion's share of the reserves' money.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: As public money will be used to co-pay a significant portion of their salaries, are there any conditions imposed on these big companies, such as they must hold off any retrenchment exercise for as long as they are receiving help from the Government?

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: And for listed companies, will there be a temporary moratorium on the payment of the dividends or share buyback exercise, once the assistance is no longer needed?

sections.label: U-Save rebates and utility charges
sections.summary: The Member asks whether U-Save rebates are adequately measured to help Singaporeans cover impending utility charge increases under stay-at-home orders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: Are the U-Save rebates adequately measured to help Singaporeans cover the impending increase in utility charges under the latest stay-at-home orders?

sections.label: Debating the Resilience Budget
sections.summary: The House is debating the $48 billion Resilience Budget, a month after the Unity Budget 2020, and a third Solidarity Budget was introduced.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Today, we are debating the Resilience Budget, a $48 billion Supplementary Budget just a month after the Unity Budget 2020 was announced.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: And we just heard the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance introduce a third Budget, the Solidarity Budget of $5.1 million.

sections.label: SGTeguhBersatu Task Force formed
sections.summary: The Malay/Muslim community has a key role, and the SGTeguhBersatu Task Force was formed with M3 agencies, Malay/Muslim organisations, NTUC and Government agencies.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Our Malay/Muslim community has a key role to play in this national effort.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: We have formed the SGTeguhBersatu Task Force, or the SG Resilience in Unity Task Force, comprising representatives from the M3 agencies, Malay/Muslim organisations, NTUC as well as Government agencies.

sections.label: Online mosque religious programmes
sections.summary: MUIS works with mosques to make more religious programmes available online via Muslim.sg and radio.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: To preserve our religious life, MUIS is working with mosques to make more religious programmes available online through Muslim.sg as well as over the radio.

sections.label: Mosques posting online content
sections.summary: More than 50 mosques acquired new digital skills and released over 130 videos online since closing on 23 March.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Many of them had to acquire entirely new digital skills to do this.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Now, more than 50 mosques have put up content online, releasing over 130 videos online since they were closed on 23 March.

sections.label: Malay/Muslim COVID-19 Working Group
sections.summary: A Malay/Muslim COVID-19 Working Group of asatizah and medical professionals was formed, co-chaired by Masagos Zulkifli and Janil Puthucheary.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Last month, we formed the Malay/Muslim COVID-19 Working Group comprising asatizah and medical professionals, co-chaired by Minister Masagos Zulkifli and Senior Minister of State Janil Puthucheary.

sections.label: SGTeguhBersatu mental wellness initiatives
sections.summary: MUIS, PPIS, PERGAS and MHPA will work together under the SGTeguhBersatu Taskforce on initiatives for psychological resilience and mental wellness.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: To spearhead this in a concrete manner, MUIS, PPIS, PERGAS and the Muslim Healthcare Professionals Association (MHPA) will be working collaboratively together, as part of the SGTeguhBersatu Taskforce, to develop initiatives and programmes to strengthen the psychological resilience and support the mental wellness of the community.

sections.label: MUIS support package for asatizah
sections.summary: MUIS has put together a comprehensive package with partners under the SGTeguhBersatu Taskforce to support asatizah during the downturn.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: To support asatizah during the downturn, I am pleased to announce that MUIS has put together a comprehensive package, together with partners, as part of the SGTeguhBersatu Taskforce.

sections.label: Asatizah upskilling with MENDAKI SENSE
sections.summary: MUIS will collaborate with MENDAKI SENSE to help asatizah upskill in IT, digital media or counselling during this downtime.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: MUIS will be collaborating with MENDAKI SENSE to help asatizah upskill during this downtime in areas, such as IT and digital media or in counselling.

sections.label: MUIS and NTUC freelance asatizah
sections.summary: MUIS will work with NTUC and accept applications from freelance asatizah who do not automatically qualify for SIRS.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: For example, MUIS will work with NTUC, and will accept applications from freelance asatizah who do not automatically qualify for the Self-Employed Person Income Relief Scheme (SIRS).

sections.label: Asatizah COVID-19 income support
sections.summary: Eligible asatizah receive three $3,000 SIRS payments from May, TRF guidance, and the COVID-19 Support Grant of $800 monthly for three months.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: As the Deputy Prime Minister had announced during his speech on the Solidary Budget earlier, asatizah who are eligible for SIRS support will receive three payments of $3,000 from May.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: MUIS will also work with MSF to guide asatizah through the Temporary Relief Fund (TRF) application process, which will provide a temporary relief of $500 for eligible asatizah who are experiencing a drop in their income due to COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Asatizah who lose their jobs due to COVID-19 can also apply for the COVID-19 Support Grant and receive $800 a month, for three months.

sections.label: MUIS grants for mosques
sections.summary: MUIS will extend grants to mosques for a 50% waiver of aLIVE fees for two months and for enhanced COVID-19 measures, costing over $1 million.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: First, in view that physical aLIVE classes will be disrupted with the closure of mosques and will be replaced by home-based learning, MUIS will extend grants to mosques to provide a 50% waiver of their aLIVE fees for two months.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: MUIS will also provide grants to mosques to support mosques to adopt the enhanced COVID-19 precautionary measures, such as temperature taking, contact tracing and queue management, when mosques reopen in the future.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: These measures to support mosques are expected to cost MUIS over $1 million.

sections.label: Shopping vouchers instead of cash
sections.summary: Shopping vouchers instead of cash could have higher value through retail consortia and a three-month validity to boost near-term spending.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Another possibility to explore is to offer shopping vouchers instead of cash.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: By working with retail consortia to exploit economies of scale, the vouchers can even have a value higher than their cash value.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: These vouchers can come with a limited validity period of perhaps three months to boost near term spending so that retailers can earn revenue sooner, and therefore, have the cash flow to retain their staff.

sections.label: Support packages for businesses
sections.summary: The Deputy Prime Minister announced new or enhanced support packages, including the Enhanced Enterprise Financing Scheme and the SME Working Capital Loan.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Even as they have to continue to pay rents, overheads and salaries, their revenue has either slowed to a trickle or come to a complete standstill.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I am, therefore, heartened by the Deputy Prime Minister's announcement today of many new or enhanced support packages, including the Enhanced Enterprise Financing Scheme and the SME Working Capital Loan.

sections.label: SMEs digital video-conferencing grants
sections.summary: SMEs shifting to digital find that Government grants do not seem to support the cost of adopting video-conferencing solutions such as Zoom.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As for SMEs that are being asked to shift their services to the digital realm, they are finding that Government grants do not seem to support the cost of adopting video-conferencing solutions such as Zoom.

sections.label: Assessing new modes of instruction
sections.summary: The passage states it is unrealistic to use old systems to assess new modes of instruction, and that innovative providers fear they will not survive and are asking for help.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It is therefore unrealistic to use old systems to assess new modes of instruction.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: They too are asking for help as they fear they will not survive this crisis, however innovative their offerings.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I hope some of these ideas can be considered and adapted to the extent that they are practicable.

sections.label: COVID-19 and Resilience Budget
sections.summary: The passage states that COVID-19 cases blew out the lights, and a qualified electrician and a Resilience Budget were brought in on 26 March.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: The lights went out as COVID-19 cases blew out the lights.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: We quickly brought in a qualified electrician and a Resilience Budget on 26 March.

sections.label: Solidarity Budget as flash light
sections.summary: The passage states the Solidarity Budget announced today provides Singaporeans a flash light to light their way in the darkness and a path out when the storm passes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: In came the Solidarity Budget that was announced today, providing Singaporeans, perhaps, with a flash light, so that we can light our way in the darkness, so that Singaporeans who may have to be at home for a month are not left without a path out when the storm passes.

sections.label: Mental health impact of COVID-19
sections.summary: The passage states the long-term mental health impact cannot be ignored, citing a Canadian mental health index drop and SARS quarantine post-traumatic stress syndrome.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Yet, we cannot ignore the long-term impact to the mental health of Singaporeans, even after the virus subsides the most recent mental health index, which is a longitudinal study in Canada, showed a dramatic 12-point drop in the overall mental health situation in Canada due to COVID-19 and the lockdown.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: We also know from SARS that quarantined persons exhibited a higher prevalence of post-traumatic stress syndrome.

sections.label: Temporary Relief Fund applicants
sections.summary: The passage describes people coming to Community Clubs to apply for the Temporary Relief Fund and worries about long-term mental health impact.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: For many of the people who have come to our Community Clubs (CCs) over the last few days to apply for the Temporary Relief Fund, I spent two days at my CC, speaking to some of them helping to process the documents as well.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: My constituency is not particularly low income but the number of people who came with large; some perhaps to try it out, but the vast majority were people from different sectors who did not expect to be so affected by this crisis.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: So, whatever we do for them now, may be a temporary stop-gap measure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: But what is more worrying is the impact on their mental health over the long term.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: So, we need to do a lot more not just during this crisis so that Singaporeans have a leg-up, so that Singaporeans know that they are not forgotten, but we also have to be prepared for the long term impact that this COVID-19 crisis will have on Singapore and Singaporeans.

sections.label: Unity, Resilience and Solidarity Budgets
sections.summary: The passage states Singaporeans must reach out to assure each other they are in this together, and hopes the Unity, Resilience and Solidarity Budgets are all that is needed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: And for us, we must constantly reach out to one another to assure each other that we are in this together, and only by being together, can we continue to be Singapore strong, that we can overcome.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: And I hope that with the Unity, the Resilience and the Solidarity Budgets – URS – yours, yours!

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Your Budget will be all that we need; that we do not need to dip in once again, that we can come out of this crisis as soon as possible and reduce the impact on Singapore and Singaporeans.

sections.label: Requests for wage and levy relief
sections.summary: Retail companies seek a higher wage offset and other relief, and gig workers are said to need help too.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Retail companies, including those downstream industries supporting tourism, are requesting to increase the wage offset under the Enhanced Jobs Support Scheme for their sector from 25% to 50%, for the remaining qualifying months beyond April.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Other feedback includes more lenient criteria for reduction or waiver of the foreign workers' levy for staff who are serving Leave of Absence or Stay-Home Notices beyond April; reducing the road tax for logistics companies and providing more rental assistance to JTC and HDB commercial tenants.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Gig workers, such as Grab delivery staff, need help, too.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: How would the Government reach out to them and auto-include them in assistance schemes?

sections.label: Bringing forward 30-30 vision
sections.summary: The 30-30 vision must be brought forward, a challenging but necessary task given Singapore imports 90% of its food.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Our 30-30 vision will have to be brought forward.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: This is a challenging but necessary task, considering that we import 90% of our food.

sections.label: Outbreak hits aviation and tourism
sections.summary: The outbreak has dealt an unprecedented blow to the aviation, transportation, entertainment, arts, tourism, hotel and catering industries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The outbreak has dealt an unprecedented blow to the aviation, transportation, entertainment, arts, tourism, hotel and catering industries.

sections.label: Residents support measures but fear starvation
sections.summary: Residents support the Government's epidemic measures but worry that people starve to death before the virus is dead.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: My residents and friends around me have expressed their understanding and full support for the many measures the Government must take to prevent the epidemic, but they are equally concerned that "people starve to death before the virus is dead" (in Hokkien).

sections.label: Durian merchants switch to selling eggs
sections.summary: Malaysia's movement control made durian picking difficult, prices plummeted, and merchants turned to selling eggs with excellent results.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Recently, because Malaysia implemented movement control, durian merchants have difficulty picking up from their suppliers, durian prices have plummeted, and the merchants, in order to survive, turned to selling eggs instead, with excellent results.

sections.label: Rethinking work, unity and investment
sections.summary: Individuals, businesses and nations must rethink work, business models and governance, stay united, and attract high-quality investments to Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Individuals, businesses and nations have to rethink the way they work, their business models and their governance policies, how to turn failures into successes, how to keep up with the times, even leaping ahead of the competition.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: We must remain united and prove to the world that we Singaporeans are resilient in order to continue to attract high-quality investments to Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I am confident that even during this crisis, we can create quality jobs for all Singaporeans and even as we fight this crisis, make good preparations for our future.

sections.label: Self-Employed Person Income Relief Scheme
sections.summary: SIRS helps Self Employed Persons over a period of nine months.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The Self-Employed Person Income Relief Scheme (SIRS) is very generous in helping Self Employed Persons (SEPs) over a period of nine months.

sections.label: Jobs Support Scheme after October
sections.summary: Business owners can use the Jobs Support Scheme to retain employees until October this year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: While business owners can leverage on the Jobs Support Scheme to retain their current employees until October this year, what will happen thereafter?

sections.label: Freezing Government fees and charges
sections.summary: Government fees and charges are frozen for one year until 31 March 2021, and late payment charges on HDB mortgage arrears are suspended.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The freezing of all Government fees and charges for one year until 31 March 2021 is a much welcomed move.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The suspension of late payment charges on HDB mortgage arrears will help many Singaporean households better manage their tight finances during this period.

sections.label: Redirection of childcare and student care fees
sections.summary: Residents asked for redirection of childcare or student care fees during the circuit-breaker period until 4 May 2020.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In addition, I have residents who have written in to ask for a redirection of childcare or student care fees during the "circuit-breaker" period until 4 May 2020.

sections.label: Support for self-employed and jobseekers
sections.summary: The Resilience Budget includes the Training Support Scheme for the self-employed and the SG United Jobs initiative with about 10,000 public sector job openings.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Among the challenges that must be addressed are related to financial issues and having enough savings to tide over this difficult economic times, especially for those who are self-employed or working freelance.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Among the initiatives and support schemes under the new Resilience Budget is the Training Support Scheme for the self-employed.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Although the Government is currently providing financial support to the self-employed, the opportunity to undergo training must also be highlighted.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: At the same time, the launch of the SG United Jobs initiative, which will provide about 10,000 public sector job openings, will present opportunities to those who are looking for permanent employment.

sections.label: Leveraging opportunities to upgrade skills
sections.summary: Individuals need to leverage opportunities to upgrade skills and expertise and continue learning to remain relevant.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: These will certainly help alleviate the hardships and challenges we face.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: But individually, we also need to start leveraging on opportunities to upgrade our skills and expertise, continue learning and re-learning, and look for opportunities so that we remain relevant.

sections.label: Community mental health suggestions
sections.summary: Speaker will raise community suggestions to cushion COVID-19 impact and build resilience, noting Resilience Budget lacked mental healthcare funding but DPM Heng acknowledged mental health support in the Solidarity Budget.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I will then raise suggestions from the communities that aim to not only cushion the immediate impact of COVID-19 but also future-proof our social and psychological resilience for a more equal and united people.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I was initially alarmed that the Resilience Budget did not allocate any funding and resources to mental healthcare, support and research for this period.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I am now slightly relieved that Deputy Prime Minister Heng acknowledged the need for mental health support as part of the national response in the Solidarity Budget announced today.

sections.label: AWARE hotline calls increase
sections.summary: AWARE received 33% more calls than usual on its Women's Hotline in the last month as social isolation measures trap victims with abusers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: AWARE has received 33% more calls than usual on its Women’s Hotline in the last month, as social isolation measures entrap victims with their abusers.

sections.label: Employer mental well-being guidance
sections.summary: Guidance should be published for all employers on supporting employees' mental well-being, and Minister Desmond Lee announced the National CARE Hotline.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Guidance should also be published for all employers on supporting their employees’ mental well-being.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I am relieved that Minister Desmond Lee announced the National CARE Hotline yesterday and he mentioned today as well.

sections.label: Residents earning under $2,000
sections.summary: In 2018, about 300,000 residents earned less than $2,000 per month.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In 2018, about 300,000 residents earned less than $2,000 per month.

sections.label: Adam's scheme payouts
sections.summary: Based on quick calculations, Adam will receive $7,632 through various schemes, including the $600 Solidarity Payment announced today.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Based on my calculations quickly, Adam will receive $7,632 through the various schemes, including the $600 Solidarity Payment that was announced today.

sections.label: Temporary Relief Fund applications
sections.summary: More than 60,000 applications have been made for the Temporary Relief Fund since applications opened last week.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: More than 60,000 applications have been made for the Temporary Relief Fund (TRF) since applications opened last week.

sections.label: Temporary Relief Fund disbursement
sections.summary: The Temporary Relief Fund and COVID-19 Support Grant could be automatically disbursed based on self-declaration or proxy indicators such as CPF contribution changes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Temporary Relief Fund and COVID-19 Support Grant could be automatically disbursed based on self-declaration or proxy indicators, such as changes in CPF contributions.

sections.label: Extending aid to families
sections.summary: The speaker proposes extending the TRF and COVID-19 Support Grant to families awaiting ComCare reviews, who are stuck in financial limbo.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As SSOs struggle with the crunch, families who need their ComCare assistance reviewed will be stuck in financial limbo.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I propose extending the TRF and COVID-19 Support Grant (CSG) to all these families to ease their cash flow at this time.

sections.label: Crowded housing and disease risk
sections.summary: There is moderate to strong evidence linking crowded housing to respiratory infectious disease risk, with at least 1,425 households of five or more in 1-room flats.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: There is moderate to strong evidence of association between crowded housing and the risk of acquiring respiratory infectious diseases.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: There are at least 1,425 households where five persons or more are crammed into a 1-room flat.

sections.label: Addressing structural inequalities and mental health
sections.summary: The speaker urges boldly addressing structural wage and housing inequalities and supporting mental health strategically through and beyond the crisis.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: But we must not let a good crisis go to waste.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We must boldly address the structural inequalities in wage and housing conditions that are clear and present, made more exigent by this crisis – because Adam and Angie are part of our own – as we must, too, with supporting the mental health of our people in a strategic and comprehensive manner through and beyond this crisis.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: If we pause and think about all that is going on, it is rather humbling to know how the tiniest of a living organism that cannot even be seen by the naked eye has such power to change us for the better by making us face our fears and flaws so that we can finally see who we are and who we are to each other.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It is up to us to choose how this horror suspense movie will end for us as a nation, because this, too, shall pass, and when it does, a more mentally resilient and equal Singapore must and will be what becomes of us.

sections.label: Government COVID-19 war chest
sections.summary: The speaker is heartened that the Government devoted a $48 billion war chest to help and support Singaporeans affected by COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As we see more and more Singaporeans getting affected by the COVID-19 situation, I am heartened and thankful that the Government has devoted a war chest of $48 billion to help and support Singaporeans.

sections.label: Prolonging JSS support for sports SMEs
sections.summary: The speaker hopes the Deputy Prime Minister considers prolonging increased JSS support past April for sports SMEs to retain employees.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: While the Resilience Budget provided for Job Support Scheme (JSS) support, these SMEs in this sector qualify for 25% on the first $4,600 of monthly salaries.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: With the Solidarity Budget, the JSS support increases to 75% for the month of April.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, most small and medium-sized sports enterprises require more support as they do not have deep pockets to sustain the business past two months in the current situation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I hope that the Deputy Prime Minister can consider prolonging the increased JSS support past April in order to help these enterprises in this affected sector to retain their employees.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: With this increased support, our sports enterprises will be able to use the opportunity to focus on re-calibrating their strategies during the downtime and emerge stronger, in a better position, to bring more benefits to Singapore and Singaporeans quicker when the situation improves.

sections.label: COVID-19 Budgets total $59.9 billion
sections.summary: The Resilience and Solidarity Budgets bring total COVID-19 support to $59.9 billion, almost a tenfold increase.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: With the Resilience and Solidarity Budgets, the total amount set aside to help Singapore and Singaporeans battle COVID-19 is now $59.9 billion – almost a tenfold increase.

sections.label: Solidarity Budget help and reserves
sections.summary: Help measures will be disbursed sooner, funded by up to $17 billion from reserves, with a $44.3 billion deficit.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: We disbursed local ComCare the next day and enrolled the children in our milk powder programme.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Hence, when I hear of the cash assistance being tripled and the introduction of various schemes such as the grocery vouchers, Temporary Relief Fund and Self-Employed Income Relief Scheme, I was very happy.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: The only request that I had at that time was to have the help disbursed sooner than later, and therefore in today's Solidarity Budget, I am pleased that some of the most essential help will be delivered within this month, much sooner than expected.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: To fund these help measures, the Government will have to, for the second time in our post-Independence history, withdraw up to $17 billion from our reserves and we can expect a total fiscal deficit of about $44.3 billion in this financial year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Just to get a sense of proportion, this deficit alone is more than half of last year's total public expenditure!

sections.label: Temporary Relief Fund overwhelms Community Centres
sections.summary: When Temporary Relief Fund applications began, Community Centres were overwhelmed on the first day.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Take, for instance, when the application for Temporary Relief Fund commenced, Community Centres were overwhelmed on the first day.

sections.label: Applicants decline skills training
sections.summary: At Community Club Temporary Relief Fund applications, some jobless or reduced-work applicants did not wish to take skills training despite incentives.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: At the Temporary Relief Fund applications at the Community Club, I observed that a number of applicants who lost their jobs or suffer reduced work do not wish to take up skills training, despite the incentives.

sections.label: Enrichment sector low technology adoption
sections.summary: Nine in 10 surveyed enrichment/education companies reported low technology adoption, predominantly using traditional teaching means.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Nine out 10 of the companies in the enrichment/education sector surveyed reported low technology adoption, meaning that they have been predominantly using the traditional means of teaching.

sections.label: Three Budgets total $59.9 billion
sections.summary: Heng Swee Keat announced Unity, Resilience and Solidarity Budgets totalling $59.9 billion, the largest since Independence, about 11% of GDP.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: To cope with the dire economic situation, Deputy Prime Minister and Finance Minister Heng Swee Keat announced three Budgets within a short span of two months, namely, Unity, Resilience and Solidarity Budget, totalling $59.9 billion, to help Singaporeans deal with the outbreak.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: This is the largest Budget since Independence, roughly 11% of our GDP.

sections.label: Reserves safeguard framework use
sections.summary: Asks whether a mechanism exists to define effective use of reserves and the amount, balancing present relief with future generations' needs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Is there a mechanism under the current reserves safeguard framework to define how we can effectively use the reserves and the amount?

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: On one hand, the amount must be sufficient to allow the Government to alleviate the situation; on the other hand, we must also ensure that our future generations will have enough funds to cope with future expenditures so that they are not left with nothing.

sections.label: Adapt and Grow training
sections.summary: Singaporeans should use the Adapt and Grow Scheme and other schemes for training and skills upgrading, and businesses should transform digitally.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: During this period, Singaporeans should make use of the Adapt and Grow Scheme as well as other schemes to undergo training, upgrade skills and be prepared for economic recovery.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: With the outbreak, businesses should also recognise the importance of digital transformation, use resources wisely and take the opportunity to transform and strengthen capabilities, and innovate continuously to stay competitive.

sections.label: Circuit breaker public concern
sections.summary: Many were concerned about the impending circuit breaker, but almost everyone understood the need and agreed to cooperate for one month.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Many were concerned about the impending "circuit breaker".

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: But almost everyone understood the need and agreed that we should all cooperate, bite the bullet and rough it out for this one month.

sections.label: Lower SIRS auto-inclusion age
sections.summary: Asks whether the Government would consider including self-employed persons aged 30 and above in automatic SIRS payouts.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The first is to lower the age for auto-inclusion for SIRS.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Automatic payout is given to eligible SEPs aged 37 and above.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Would the Government consider including SEPs aged 30 and above as well?

sections.label: COVID-19 Support Grant eligibility
sections.summary: Suggests unemployed residents actively job-hunting or in training should also be assisted under the COVID-19 Support Grant.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Second, some unemployed residents hope to qualify for the COVID-19 Support Grant, which was targeted at employees who lost their jobs due to the contagion.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: While they had not lost their jobs earlier due to COVID-19, the crisis has definitely made their ongoing search for jobs much harder.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I feel that as long as they are actively looking for jobs, whether these are permanent or part-time positions or on fixed term contracts, or are still attending training, they should be also assisted under this scheme.

sections.label: Solidarity Budget announcement
sections.summary: Deputy Prime Minister Heng announced the Solidarity Budget today.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Today, Deputy Prime Minister Heng announced the Solidarity Budget.

sections.label: SGUnited Traineeship and Jobs Initiatives
sections.summary: The Government announced the SGUnited Traineeship Programmes and the SGUnited Jobs Initiative.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: In this regard, the Government has announce the SGUnited Traineeship Programmes and the SGUnited Jobs Initiative.

sections.label: Resilience Budget and relief measures
sections.summary: The $48 billion Resilience Budget brought relief, with measures like the Temporary Relief Fund and proposed laws on property tax rebates and contractual obligations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: The extensive $48 billion Resilience Budget therefore came as a much welcomed relief.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Details of the specific measures have come in and we have started to roll out some of these measures like the Temporary Relief Fund.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: For example, the proposed new law to compel landlords to pass on property tax rebate to tenants and the proposed law to provide relief to parties with contractual obligations and have difficulties performing them because of COVID-19.

sections.label: Further $4 billion from Reserves
sections.summary: Deputy Prime Minister Heng announced in-principle approval from President Halimah Yacob to draw down a further $4 billion from the Reserves.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Deputy Prime Minister Heng has announced that he has gotten in-principle approval from President Halimah Yacob to draw down a further $4 billion from our Reserves on top of the earlier $17 billion dollars that was approved.

sections.label: Employers, employees and landlords support
sections.summary: Employers should use the Enhanced Jobs Support Scheme, employees should support businesses, and landlords should pass on property tax rebates to tenants.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Employers should tap on Government support like the Enhanced Jobs Support Scheme to retain their employees and let them continue to earn a living.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Employees need to be understanding and help support the businesses where necessary so that there will still be a job to go to after this crisis is over.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Landlords should work alongside tenants to help them retain the premises and pass on the property tax rebates to their tenants.

sections.label: Public hygiene and SG Clean
sections.summary: Public hygiene has come to the forefront, and SGClean offers the opportunity to make the vision of a clean Singapore a reality.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: We have spoken about wanting to make Singapore clean, educate people with better social habits, how we want to be like Japan.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Now, public hygiene has come to the forefront and we have the opportunity with SGClean to make this vision a reality.

sections.label: Jobs Support Scheme wage co-funding
sections.summary: The Jobs Support Scheme co-funds the first $4,600 of gross monthly wages for nine months, at 75% for April, but not for business owners trading in personal capacity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Under the Jobs Support Scheme, JSS, the Government will co-fund the first $4,600 of gross monthly wages paid to each local employee for nine months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: For April, the co-funding is 75% of the employee's monthly wages, up to $4,600.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: However, IRAS' website says that the wages paid to business owners or employers trading in their personal capacity will not be eligible for the payout.

sections.label: Review of SEP help criteria
sections.summary: The speaker urges the Deputy Prime Minister to review the criteria for help to eligible self-employed persons, despite announced enhancements and a higher property annual value of $21,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Next, while I appreciate the announcement by the Deputy Prime Minister yesterday to enhance the help given to eligible self-employed and to increase the annual value of the properties to $21,000, may I urge the Deputy Prime Minister to review the criteria?

sections.label: Appeals for self-employed in condominiums
sections.summary: The speaker urges the Government to allow case-by-case appeals and assist self-employed persons who run retail shops, are housing agents or run tuition agencies but get no JSS help because they live in a more expensive condominium.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: So, for the SEPs who run retail shops, if they are self-employed housing agents, if they run their own tuition agencies, they will earn nothing this month and yet not receive any help under the JSS, just because they live in a more expensive condominium.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: So, I urge the Government to allow appeals on a case-by-case basis and to render assistance to this group of people during this difficult time.

sections.label: Supplementary Budgets share of GDP
sections.summary: The Supplementary Budgets, the Resilience and Solidarity Budgets, amount to 12% of GDP and close to $60 billion, which the speaker says lies probably in the middle ground.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: At 12% of our GDP and close to $60 billion, our Supplementary Budgets – the Resilience and now the Solidarity Budgets – lies probably in the middle ground.

sections.label: Deferral of residential property loan repayments
sections.summary: MAS has announced that homeowners may apply to defer repayments on their residential property loans until the end of the year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: For many of us, one of our biggest monthly expenditures is mortgage repayments on our homes and MAS has announced that homeowners may apply to defer repayments for their residential property loans until the end of the year.

sections.label: Interest on deferred loan payments
sections.summary: No interest will be charged on deferred interest payments, but interest will continue to accrue on the deferred principal amounts.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: No interest will be charged on the deferred interest payments.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: However, they must take note that interest will continue to accrue on the deferred principal amounts.

sections.label: SEP scheme monthly payouts
sections.summary: Under this scheme, self-employed persons will receive $1,000 a month for a total of nine months.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Of course, currently, we now know that under this scheme, SEPs will receive $1,000 a month for a total of nine months.

sections.label: MediSave and medication subsidies
sections.summary: Asks whether MediSave can be used for medical care and whether MAF and MAF Plus subsidies for costly medications can be raised above 50% to 85%.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: MediSave has also been looked upon as every citizen’s individual reserves for medical care, and surely the current economic climate provides a mandate to dip into this personal cash reserve for necessary medical use?

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Next, for the Medication Assistance Fund – both the MAF and MAF Plus – would the Government or MOH consider increasing the level of subsidy for more costly medications, up from the current band of between 50% and 85%?

sections.label: Deferring premiums, MediSave, MediFund
sections.summary: Notes policyholders may defer premiums six months and asks if SEPs can defer MediSave instalments and if MediFund criteria can be loosened temporarily.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Insurance policyholders can now apply to defer premium payments for up to six months while maintaining insurance coverage.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: In addition, would MOM consider allowing SEPs to defer their MediSave instalment payments during the current climate of economic difficulties?

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Last but not least, I hope that the eligibility criteria for MediFund will be loosened temporarily during this contagion period to assist patients who may not qualify during more regular periods.

sections.label: Temporary Relief Fund applications
sections.summary: Minister Desmond Lee noted last week that 60,000 Singaporeans have applied for the Temporary Relief Fund.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Minister Desmond Lee noted last week that 60,000 Singaporeans have applied for the Temporary Relief Fund.

sections.label: Solidarity Budget cash payment
sections.summary: The Solidarity Budget's $600 cash payment to all adult Singaporeans will make a significant difference, along with the Temporary Relief Fund and other support measures.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Solidarity Budget’s cash payment of $600 to all adult Singaporeans will make a significant difference, as will the Temporary Relief Fund, and other financial support measures.

sections.label: Proposal for weekly payments
sections.summary: Proposes paying $110 per week to all Singaporeans for 12 weeks, starting immediately if possible, through existing electronic payment channels.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Our initial proposal is to pay $110 per week to all Singaporeans for a period of 12 weeks, starting immediately if possible, through existing electronic payment channels for Government's cash transfers to Singaporeans’ bank accounts.

sections.label: MUBI tax increase
sections.summary: Taxes financing the payouts are paid next year, and MUBI requires a temporary personal income tax increase of 4.25%, with the bottom half of taxpayers benefiting.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: But the taxes to finance those payouts will only be paid next year, according to the usual schedule for tax payment.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We have calculated that MUBI requires a temporary personal income tax increase of 4.25%.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Even after the tax, the bottom half of taxpayers will benefit.

sections.label: MUBI payouts and tax costs
sections.summary: A $110 weekly MUBI payout covers basic expenses for most vulnerable households, with tax increment raising $4.467 billion against $4.62 billion projected costs.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Based on the data, a MUBI payout of $110 per week, per citizen, is sufficient to cover basic living expenses in these categories of at least 60% of all households.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The actual average per-capita expenditure is $105 per week and two-thirds of this is on food.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Their estimated costs in these categories for elderly households were similar to ours.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: So, we believe that payouts of $110 per week, per person, will cover the most vulnerable Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Based on Year of Assessment 2018 tax data, the MUBI temporary tax increment will raise $4.467 billion, which is just short of projected MUBI scheme costs of $4.62 billion.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: But the Government will also have to absorb the risk that tax collections next year will be much lower than expected, if the recovery is slow and prolonged.

sections.label: MUBI payouts for taxpayers
sections.summary: A lower income taxpayer earning $30,000 receives $1,320 in MUBI payouts but owes $200 more in taxes.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For example, let us look at a lower income taxpayer, who earns about $30,000 a year.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: They will receive $1,320 in MUBI payouts this year and they will owe about $200 more in taxes the next year.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For the median taxpayer, who earns about $58,000 a year, the MUBI benefit is just $100 more than the temporary tax increase.

sections.label: MUBI payouts with dependents
sections.summary: A median income taxpayer with two dependents gets nearly $4,000 in MUBI payouts but pays about $1,200 in tax.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Nearly half of Singaporeans, such as our children, elderly and homemakers, pay no income tax.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This means that a median income taxpayer with two dependents would get a total MUBI payout of nearly $4,000 this year, but only pay about $1,200 in tax the next year on this.

sections.label: Median taxpayer keeps payouts
sections.summary: The median taxpayer with two dependents keeps 95% of payouts if they lose half their income.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The median taxpayer with two dependents keeps 95% of the payouts if they were to lose half of their income during the year.

sections.label: Universal cash payments rationale
sections.summary: The MUBI scheme makes universal cash payments for basic daily living expenses because COVID-19's impact cannot be predicted.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The MUBI scheme therefore makes cash payments on universal basis to cover basic daily living expenses, because we cannot predict which Singaporean will be affected by the COVID-19 pandemic next and to what extent.

sections.label: Solidarity Budget spending
sections.summary: The Solidarity Budget proposes $5.1 billion to save jobs and support businesses and families, with $4 billion from Reserves.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: The Solidarity Budget proposes that another $5.1 billion be spent to save jobs, support businesses and families during these extraordinary four weeks, with $4 billion of that coming from our Reserves.

sections.label: Singapore unemployment and reserves
sections.summary: MP asks the Deputy Prime Minister about Singapore's unemployment outlook and whether there is a limit to tapping reserves.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: In the US, the COVID-19 "freeze" is expected to cost 47 million jobs and send the unemployment rate past 32%, according to St Louis Fed projections.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: With such grave outcomes being predicted in other parts of the world, I would like to ask Deputy Prime Minister about his outlook on Singapore's unemployment – both the base case as well as worst case scenarios?

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Even as we work relentlessly to mitigate the scale of retrenchment and rise in unemployment, I would like to ask Deputy Prime Minister whether he has in mind a limit to which the reserves should be tapped?

sections.label: Enterprise Singapore F&B package
sections.summary: Enterprise Singapore's recently launched package funds 5% of commission costs to support F&B players.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Some relief is provided by the recently launched Enterprise Singapore’s package to support F&B players by funding 5% of the commission cost.

sections.label: SME loans and landlord rebates
sections.summary: MP notes new laws compel landlords to pass on property tax rebates and asks MAS to prescribe lower SME loan interest rates.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: I hope such solutions will be developed by businesses themselves, without depending on the heavy hand of the Government or the law.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: It is regrettable that we have to enact new laws to compel landlords to pass on property tax rebates to tenants.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: The relief package offered by banks and insurers, to defer repayment of loans as well as insurance premiums until the end of the year, will be a lifeline for many impacted.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: It will also help financial institutions reduce risks of delinquencies and bankruptcies, by sharing the burden of debt with individuals and SMEs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: However, I was surprised to hear from Senior Minister of State Chee Hong Tat during a Parliamentary Question yesterday, that the SME Working Capital Loan Programme has so far helped only 662 enterprises and the Temporary Bridging Loan interest rate is as much as 5% despite the Government’s risk-sharing at 80%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: This contrasts poorly with Switzerland’s crisis loan scheme to SMEs, where over 76,000 small businesses availed themselves of more than SFr 15 billion in the first week of launch, at zero interest.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: With these strong Government interventions, I would like to ask if MAS can prescribed a much lower interest rate chargeable such that there is more take up, and boost SMEs chances of surviving this storm and ease their recovery with less debt burden.

sections.label: Arts and Culture Resilience Package
sections.summary: Fifty-five million dollars has been set aside for an Arts and Culture Resilience Package under the Resilience Budget.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Fifty-five million dollars has been set aside for an Arts and Culture Resilience Package (ACRP) as part of the Resilience Budget.

sections.label: Freelancer and wage support
sections.summary: Eligible arts or sports freelancers may receive up to $12,000, and the Government will co-fund 25% of local wages under the enhanced JSS.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Depending on individual circumstances, an eligible arts or sports freelancer may potentially receive $12,000 from May to October 2020 from SIRS and the Enhanced Workfare Special Payment among the broad-based measures in the Resilience and Solidarity Budgets, even before factoring other schemes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: For companies, the Deputy Prime Minister announced that the Government will co-fund 25% of the wages of every local employee under the enhanced Jobs Support Scheme or JSS, which will last till end 2020, and 75% for the month of April, in view of the heightened measures.

sections.label: Sports sector temporary jobs
sections.summary: Over 500 temporary sports sector job opportunities have been identified under the SGUnited Jobs Initiative.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: To further support employment in the sports sector, as part of the SGUnited Jobs Initiative, we have identified more than 500 temporary job opportunities for various roles in the sports sector to support our national sports associations (NSAs), sports centres, academy and clubs as well as to support digital and exercise-science related capabilities.

sections.label: Sports training and coach grant
sections.summary: More training programmes will be made available in the sports sector, and the Coach Development Grant rises to $100,000 from $30,000.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: We will progressively make more training programmes available to individuals in the sports sector.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: We will also set aside $100,000 for the Coach Development Grant, up from $30,000 in previous years, to cover coaches’ registration and course fees when they sign up for CCE courses.

sections.label: Enhanced CDSA arts training support
sections.summary: NAC will list more online courses eligible for CDSA support, with enhanced amounts for companies, arts groups and up to 6,000 freelancers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: In the coming months, NAC will list more online courses which are eligible for CDSA support.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: We have enhanced the CDSA so that Major Companies can now receive up to $20,000 for training, while other arts groups can receive up to $6,000.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: In addition to organisations and their employees, we will also support the training of up to 6,000 freelancers through the CDSA.

sections.label: Freelancer training support amounts
sections.summary: Freelancers can receive up to $1,000 for training, covering course fee subsidies and a $10 per hour training allowance.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Our freelancers can receive up to $1,000 for their training, which can cover both course fee subsidies and a training allowance of $10 per hour.

sections.label: New Digital Presentation Grant
sections.summary: NAC will offer a new Digital Presentation Grant of up to $20,000 per project to digitalise arts and culture content and delivery.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: NAC will offer a new Digital Presentation Grant for the arts of up to $20,000 per project, to ramp up efforts in digitalisation of arts and culture content and delivery.

sections.label: Digital arts offerings and demand
sections.summary: NAC aims to roll out digital arts offerings, support over 200 new digital projects and create more than 1,000 opportunities after circuit breaker measures are relaxed.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: We hope to roll out digital offerings by our arts groups in the coming months through multiple platforms and festivals.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: We aim to generate demand for the arts and culture sector, support over 200 new digital projects, and create more than 1,000 opportunities for our cultural and related practitioners once the circuit breaker measures are relaxed.

sections.label: Sports digital content grant
sections.summary: A new $2 million grant will support more than 50 projects for sports SEPs and businesses to develop digital and virtual content.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Singapore, we will also offer a new $2 million grant to support more than 50 projects for sports SEPs and businesses to develop initiatives that create digital and virtual content and provide innovative ways to deliver sports for Singaporeans to stay active and fit in the lead-up from now to National Day in August.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: (In Mandarin):   In this challenging period, MCCY will strive to help our arts, culture and sports sector overcome the impact brought about by COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: We will introduce a $55 million Arts and Culture Resilience Package (ACRP) to help protect jobs and maintain livelihoods.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: First, Deputy Prime Minister had earlier announced that the Government will co-fund 25% of the wages of every local employee under the enhanced Jobs Support Scheme (JSS) till end of this year, and 75% for the month of April when "circuit breaker" measures are in place.

sections.label: Rental waiver and arts scheme
sections.summary: Eligible tenants in MCCY-owned properties get two months of rental waiver, and NAC's Capability Development Scheme for the Arts is enhanced to benefit more arts and culture organisations and practitioners, including freelancers, up to end of 2020.
