sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Next, all eligible tenants in MCCY-owned properties will benefit from the two months of rental waiver, to help lower their costs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: As such, we will enhance the National Arts Council’s (NAC's) one-time Capability Development Scheme for the Arts (CDSA) to benefit more arts and culture organisations and practitioners, including freelancers, up to end of 2020.

sections.label: Jobs Support Scheme wage support
sections.summary: Under the Resilience Budget, the Jobs Support Scheme gave aviation and tourism 75% and F&B 50% wage support up to the first $4,600 of each staff wage for nine months, while remaining businesses received a flat 25%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Under the Resilience Budget, the Jobs Support Scheme extended greater assistance to specified sectors, such as aviation and tourism and F&B sectors, giving 75% and 50% support for wages up to the first $4,600 of each of their staff wages for these respective sectors for nine months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The remaining businesses only received a flat 25% of their staff wages up to the first $4,600.

sections.label: Solidarity Budget wage support boost
sections.summary: Wage support under the Jobs Support Scheme in the Solidarity Budget was boosted to 75% for all businesses for April, which may only mitigate part of losses from the month-long workplace closure starting today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: While the wage support for the Jobs Support Scheme under the Solidarity Budget has been boosted to 75% for all businesses for the solitary month of April and will be welcomed by all, for many businesses, it may only mitigate part of the losses expected from the enforced month-long closure of workplaces starting today.

sections.label: JSS excludes shareholder employees
sections.summary: The Jobs Support Scheme does not apply to employees who are shareholders, partners or sole proprietors of businesses even though they may take a salary as an employee of the business.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The JSS is not applicable to one category of employees – employees who are shareholders, partners or sole proprietors of businesses even though they may take a salary as an employee of the business.

sections.label: SEP Income Relief Scheme exclusion
sections.summary: The Self-Employed Person Income Relief Scheme does not apply to them as the scheme stipulates that there should not be any employee income.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Self-Employed Person Income Relief Scheme is not applicable to them as the scheme stipulates that there should not be any employee income.

sections.label: Pre-school fee refunds
sections.summary: It was announced that all pre-school operators are to provide 50% refund of net school fees for non-attendance during the circuit breaker period.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Yesterday, it was announced that all pre-school operators are to provide 50% refund of net school fees for non-attendance during the circuit breaker period.

sections.label: Refunds versus JSS wage support
sections.summary: The passage states that in some cases total refunds will likely be higher than the 75% wage support received through the JSS.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In some cases, the total refunds will likely be higher than the 75% wage support received by way of the JSS.

sections.label: Self-Employed Person Income Relief Scheme criteria
sections.summary: The Self-Employed Person Income Relief Scheme will be open to those earning net trade income of no more than $100,000, living in a property with an annual value originally no more than $13,000, and not owning two or more properties, with the $13,000 limit raised to $21,000 yesterday.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Self-Employed Person Income Relief Scheme will be open to those who earn a net trade income of no more than $100,000, live in a property with an annual value of no more than $13,000 originally and do not own two or more properties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: While it is good that the $13,000 annual value limit has since been raised to $21,000 yesterday.

sections.label: Relief fund conditions and landlord savings
sections.summary: A private hire car driver asked whether the Special Relief Fund can be paid directly to all registered private hire drivers, and questions were raised on ensuring tenants and sub-tenants share property tax rebate and rental waiver savings, including for coffeeshop store-holders and elderly hawkers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: A private hire car driver also shared with us at our Meet-the-People Session in Hougang last week that the incentives that come together with the Special Relief Fund may come with conditions imposed by his company that are impossible to fulfill in this economic climate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: He asked whether the Special Relief Fund can be paid directly to all registered private hire drivers instead.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: On the issue of landlords passing on savings from the property tax rebate and rental waivers granted under the Unity and Resilience Budgets, I am glad that the measures are being taken to ensure landlords' cooperation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: However, I would like to ask what measures are being taken to ensure that tenants will share any property tax rebate or rental waiver savings they obtain from landlords with their sub-tenants, including the newly announced increase in rental waivers for Government-owned properties?

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Now, be they tenants or sub-tenants of Government-owned, private, commercial, industrial or office properties, what can sub-tenants do to ensure that they get to enjoy any rental rebate passed on to the tenants by the landlords?

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Are coffeeshop store-holders in this position as well?

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: For example, could the Government look into whether they could take more measures to ensure that these elderly hawkers and workers will have better protective equipment and safer working environment?

sections.label: Supplementary Budget surplus questions
sections.summary: Questions were asked about the $48 billion Supplementary Budget and $4 billion of enhancements, how much was obtained from drawing on the surplus, whether the surplus was fully drawn, and how much came from other sources.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: On that note, I would like to ask the Finance Minister of the $48 billion Supplementary Budget and the $4 billion of enhancements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I believe that was $21 billion, which begs the next question.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: How much was obtained from drawing on the surplus from this term of government?

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Thirdly, has the surplus been drawn upon fully with this Supplementary Budget?

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: And fourthly, how much was obtained from other sources and what are those sources?

sections.label: Deferred rent repayment assurances
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Government will provide clear assurances that it will consider very much extended deferment where deferred rent cannot be paid back and there is evidence of the company's viability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In cases where deferred rent cannot be paid back, will the Government provide clear assurances that it will consider providing very much extended deferment where there is evidence of the company's viability.

sections.label: Mailing reusable masks
sections.summary: The passage asks whether reusable masks can at least be mailed to those who prefer to receive them by mail if the Government does not want to mail masks out.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: If the Government does not want to mail these masks out, can we at least arrange to mail reusable masks to those who prefer to receive them by mail.

sections.label: Powers to compel domestic firms
sections.summary: The passage asks what powers the Government has to compel domestic firms here to do the same.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: What powers does the Government have to compel domestic firms here to do the same?

sections.label: ICU beds per capita comparison
sections.summary: The passage asks how ICU beds per capita compare with other countries and whether the crisis can be used to plan expansion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: How does our number of ICU beds per capita compare with other countries?

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Can we use this crisis to formulate plans to expand ICU beds at short notice at acute care facilities with plans to work with the private sector and retired professionals to augment the supply of equipment and personnel in a time of crisis?

sections.label: Wearing masks out of doors
sections.summary: The passage states that the minority of naysayers who had called for wearing masks out of doors from an early stage had a valid point.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Let us look at the question of wearing masks out of doors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: It now seems that the minority of naysayers who had called for that from an early stage onwards at a valid point – like the four doctors who signed an open letter to that effect in February.

sections.label: Openness, transparency, debate, accountability
sections.summary: The passage states that many were wrong-footed, including the World Health Organization, and calls for openness, transparency, debate and accountability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Many of us were wrong-footed on this question including the World Health Organization, but that points to the continuing value of openness, transparency, debate and accountability even in times of crisis.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Let us debate big questions openly, rationally, sensibly, on the basis of transparency to define an agreed set of relevant facts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Let us accept that there can be different goals and strategies that are consistent with the same facts, not labelling those with different views about those goals and strategies.

sections.label: Temporary Relief Fund and COVID-19 Support Grant
sections.summary: The passage states the Temporary Relief Fund provides a one-off $500 cash grant and proposes expanding the COVID-19 Support Grant.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The only new scheme applicable to this group of workers in this Budget is the Temporary Relief Fund.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: But it only provides one-off cash grant of $500.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: For a start, we can expand the COVID-19 Support Grant to supplement the monthly income of these workers up to a cap of $800 and up to three months or when they are back to full employment.

sections.label: Government-paid childcare leave for parents
sections.summary: The passage expresses hope to introduce Government-paid childcare leave for parents in essential services or key economic sectors affected by COVID-related stay-home requirements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: To help such parents, I hope we can introduce a Government-paid childcare leave for parents who are working in essential services or key economic sectors and whose children are affected by COVID-related stay-home requirements.

sections.label: Single unwed parents eligibility
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Government can confirm that single unwed parents qualify.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Government confirm that single unwed parents qualify?

sections.label: Migrant worker dorm conditions
sections.summary: The passage states that photos from migrant workers in a dorm show conditions still far from optimal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Last night, I received photos from migrant workers living in one of these dorms and the conditions are still far from optimal.

sections.label: Quarantined workers paid leave
sections.summary: The passage states MOM will work with employers so quarantined workers are paid and their absence treated as paid hospitalisation leave.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Minister Josephine has said that MOM will work with employers to ensure that quarantined workers continue to be paid and that their period of absence from work is treated as paid hospitalisation leave, as part of the workers' statutory leave eligibility.

sections.label: Foreign Worker Levy rebates
sections.summary: The passage asks whether levy rebates will reach workers and how salaries will be paid rather than unpaid leave.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Deputy Prime Minister Heng also announced yesterday that we will waive the monthly Foreign Worker Levy due in April and also provide employers with a Foreign Worker Levy Rebate of $750 for each work permit or S Pass holder.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can I ask whether we will be ensuring that these rebates are passed down to the workers and how will we ensure that the workers are paid their salaries and not put on unpaid leave?

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: As we march forward with this Supplementary Budget that targets aid at specific groups, we must make sure that no one slip through the cracks.

sections.label: Workplace closures from today
sections.summary: The passage states that from today all workplaces are closed except essential services or key economic sectors.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: From today, all workplaces, with the exception of those in essential services or key economic sectors, are closed.

sections.label: Work-Life Grant enhancements
sections.summary: The passage states MOM will enhance the Work-Life Grant, reducing telecommuting and staggered hours requirements from six months to one month.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: Furthermore, working from home has allowed parents to deal with school issues and gives many of us leeway in handling other disruptions." Today, companies can already benefit from MOM's Work-Life Grant (WLG) and receive $2,000 for every worker who adopts an FWA.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: MOM will enhance the WLG parameters by reducing the requirement for firms to have their workers telecommute and be on staggered hours – from a minimum period of six months to just one month.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: The enhanced WLG parameters will apply after the mandatory circuit breaker period comes to an end and the grant will be open for application on 20 April 2020.

sections.label: Firms retraining workers through programmes
sections.summary: Over 100 firms applied, with over 2,600 workers expected to benefit from retraining programmes like Place-and-Train.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: More than 100 firms have already applied, with more than 2,600 workers expected to benefit from this move.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: For instance, SITA World Travel (SITA) equipped their staff through various courses with skills like data analytics and event management.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: Two employees are on the new Digital Marketing Place-and-Train Programme and they will be redeployed to support SITA’s online platform with their newly acquired skills.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: This hotel is also tapping on MOM’s enhanced measures to retrain close to 50 of their employees through the Job Redesign Place-and-Train programme for the hotel industry.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: Their 50 staff will acquire deeper capabilities in hotel operations, with the aim of taking on an expanded job scope.

sections.label: Three Budgets in seven weeks
sections.summary: In seven weeks, Deputy Prime Minister Heng Swee Keat delivered three Budgets: Unity, Resilience and Solidarity.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: In just seven weeks, we saw and we heard from Deputy Prime Minister Heng Swee Keat, he delivered three Budgets – the Unity Budget, the Resilience Budget and yesterday the Solidarity Budget.

sections.label: Resilience Budget draws on reserves
sections.summary: The Resilience Budget requires Parliament to make a significant decision because it draws on reserves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The Resilience Budget requires a significant decision on the part of Parliament as it draws on our reserves.

sections.label: Aviation sector support and job scheme
sections.summary: The aviation sector receives $350 million enhanced support, besides a job support scheme offsetting 75% of the first $4,600 of local wages.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Besides supporting workers through the additional job support scheme to offset 75% of the first $4,600 of a local employee’s wages, the aviation sector is receiving $350 million enhanced aviation support.

sections.label: 2019 international visitor arrivals and spending
sections.summary: In 2019, Singapore had 19.1 million international visitor arrivals who spent an estimated $27.1 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In 2019,	there were 19.1 million international visitor arrivals	in Singapore who spent an estimated $27.1 billion.

sections.label: Property tax rebates broadened
sections.summary: The Unity Budget gave qualifying commercial properties a 15% property tax rebate, and the Resilience Budget broadened its quantum and scope.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In the Unity Budget, qualifying commercial properties were given 15% property tax rebate, with the landlords urged to pass this on to their tenants.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In	the Resilience Budget, the quantum and scope was broadened.

sections.label: Passing on property tax rebate
sections.summary: The speaker suggests making it compulsory for commercial landlords to pass the full property tax rebate in actual dollar terms to tenants, and legislation is soon being passed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Beyond my suggested declaration, we should make it compulsory for the commercial landlord to pass on the full property tax rebate, in actual dollar terms, to the tenants.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Hence, I am glad that we are soon passing legislation to that effect.

sections.label: Financing support for businesses
sections.summary: The Resilience Budget supports businesses through financing such as the Temporary Bridging Loan Programme, and the Solidarity Budget seeks to raise the Government's risk share from 80% to 90%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: One of the ways the Resilience Budget supports businesses is by helping them get the financing that they need, for example, through the Temporary Bridging Loan Programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Indeed,	the	Solidarity	Budget	seeks	to	increase	the Government’s risk share from 80% to 90%.

sections.label: Volunteer and donation offers
sections.summary: A person wants to volunteer delivering food to the elderly, and a constituent named Darren emailed that his family wants to donate $30,000 to help vulnerable residents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: She shared with me that she wants to help as a volunteer to deliver food for the elderly in the constituency.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: And	just yesterday, I received a message from a constituent named Darren, who emailed me saying that his family wants to donate $30,000 to a worthy cause in the constituency to help the more vulnerable residents tide over this period.

sections.label: SEP Income Relief Scheme payouts
sections.summary: SIRS was introduced in the Resilience Budget and enhanced in the Solidarity Budget, giving eligible Singaporean SEPs three quarterly cash payouts of $3,000 each, $9,000 in total.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: To help Singaporean SEPs with less means and family support tide through this period of extraordinary economic uncertainty, we introduced the SEP Income Relief Scheme (SIRS) as part of the Resilience Budget and enhanced it in the Solidarity Budget.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: All eligible Singaporean SEPs will receive direct cash assistance through three quarterly cash payouts of $3,000 each or $9,000 in total.

sections.label: STSS extension and allowance increase
sections.summary: The Government has extended the STSS till the end of the year and will increase the hourly training allowance from $7.50 to $10 with effect from 1 May 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: The Government has now extended the STSS till the end of the year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: We will also increase the hourly training allowance from $7.50 to $10, with effect from 1 May 2020.

sections.label: Enhanced WSP for low-wage workers
sections.summary: WSP will be enhanced for low-wage workers, including SEPs, earning up to $2,000 per month in 2019, who will receive $3,000 each fully in cash.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: We will enhance WSP to step up support for our low-wage workers, including SEPs, earning up to $2,000 per month in 2019.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: They will receive an enhanced WSP of $3,000 each, fully in cash.

sections.label: Increased fund support for workers
sections.summary: From 1 April, fund support rose to up to two months' salary capped at $4,600, and coverage extended to half the workforce.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Since 1 April this year, we have increased the support from the fund, from up to one month’s salary, capped at $1,000 today, to up to two months’ salary, capped at $4,600, depending on the worker’s income.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: To help more workers, we have extended the coverage of the fund beyond the low-wage workers to cover half of the workforce.

sections.label: Dormitories gazetted as isolation areas
sections.summary: Due to COVID-19, the Ministry of Health gazetted S11 Dormitory @ Punggol and Westlite Toh Guan Dormitory as isolation areas two days ago.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: As Members would all know now, as a result of the evolving COVID-19 situation, the Ministry of Health gazetted the S11 Dormitory @ Punggol and Westlite Toh Guan Dormitory as isolation areas two days ago.

sections.label: Foreign worker levy waiver and rebate
sections.summary: With the levy waiver and rebate measures, foreign workers can be assured employers should continue paying salaries, accommodation and food.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: With Deputy Prime Minister Heng’s announcement of the foreign worker levy waiver and rebate measures, we can now give our foreign workers greater assurance that their employers should be able to continue to pay for their salaries, provide accommodation and food.

sections.label: Cash payouts for eligible SEPs
sections.summary: Eligible Singaporean SEPs will receive quarterly cash payouts of $3,000 each, totalling $9,000.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Eligible Singaporean SEPs will receive quarterly cash payouts of $3,000 each, or $9,000 in total.

sections.label: Training allowances and Workfare Special Payment
sections.summary: SEPs have no cap on training and can get $800 monthly allowances; lower wage workers receive a $3,000 Workfare Special Payment in cash over two tranches.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: There is no cap to how much training SEPs can sign up for.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: So, an SEP like freelancers, taxi drivers or private hire car drivers, who joins a full-time course, which is 8 hours for 10 days for instance, will receive an allowance of $800 per month.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: We will also help our lower wage workers as well.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: They will receive a Workfare Special Payment of $3,000, fully in cash over two tranches.

sections.label: SGUnited Jobs Initiative job creation
sections.summary: The SGUnited Jobs Initiative will create about 10,000 jobs over the next one year from the public and private sectors.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: The SGUnited Jobs Initiative will create about 10,000 jobs over the next one year that will come from both the public and private sectors.

sections.label: SGUnited Jobs vacancies and applicants
sections.summary: As at 2 April, about 3,900 vacancies are available and more than 5,400 jobseekers have applied for SGUnited Jobs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: As at 2 April, there are about 3,900 vacancies available, and more than 5,400 jobseekers have applied for SGUnited Jobs.

sections.label: SGUnited Traineeships programme support
sections.summary: The SGUnited Traineeships programme will support employers to offer traineeships instead for fresh graduates.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: The SGUnited Traineeships programme will provide employers with support to offer traineeships instead for fresh graduates.

sections.label: Temporary Relief Fund applications
sections.summary: MSF rolled out the Temporary Relief Fund last Wednesday, a one-off $500 cash disbursement, with more than 100,000 applications received so far.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Last Wednesday, MSF rolled out the Temporary Relief Fund (TRF) for those who need immediate assistance in April.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: This is a one-off cash disbursement of $500.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: We have received more than 100,000 applications so far.

sections.label: COVID-19 Support Grant details
sections.summary: Applicants can download forms to drop off at SSO or CC, and the COVID-19 Support Grant provides $800 monthly for three months during job search or retraining.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Applicants can also download application forms from the website, fill them at home and drop it off later at any SSO or CC without having to queue.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Those who have lost their jobs due to retrenchment or have had their employment contract terminated as a result of this crisis, will be supported by the COVID-19 Support Grant (CSG), which has a longer runway.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: It will provide a grant of $800 per month, for three months, while applicants participate in a job search or retraining programme.

sections.label: Longer ComCare support for new cases
sections.summary: Longer ComCare support is also provided for new cases, typically around six months.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Longer ComCare support is also provided for new cases – typically around six months.

sections.label: Courage Fund donations
sections.summary: The Community Chest has received more than $8 million in donations to The Courage Fund for healthcare and frontline workers and lower income families affected by COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: The Community Chest has received more than $8 million of donations to The Courage Fund, to support our healthcare and frontline workers, and lower income families affected by COVID-19.

sections.label: Invictus Fund for vulnerable persons
sections.summary: NCSS will set up The Invictus Fund, built from private donations, to support vulnerable people.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Many have been working hard to help vulnerable persons, but their donations and fund-raising efforts have been significantly diminished, at a time when they really need to find new ways and bring in new technologies to continue to reach out, to assure and to support vulnerable people in these difficult times.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: So, the National Council for Social Service or NCSS, will be setting up a new fund, The Invictus Fund, which will be built up from private donations.

sections.label: Cash support for adult Singaporeans
sections.summary: Under the Solidarity Budget, adult Singaporeans will receive $600 of cash support in April.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Under the Solidarity Budget that Deputy Prime Minister announced yesterday, adult Singaporeans will receive $600 of cash support in April.

sections.label: National CARE Hotline emotional support
sections.summary: A National CARE Hotline will be set up to offer emotional support to anyone facing stress or anxiety.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Hence, beyond financial and material support, we must shore up our own emotional and psychological well-being and enmesh this sense of community, that we are all in this together.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: We will set up a National CARE Hotline to offer emotional support to anyone who faces stress, are anxious, or simply need someone to talk to.

sections.label: Temporary Relief Fund and Support Grant
sections.summary: The TRF received over 100,000 applications in four days, and the COVID-19 Support Grant gives $800 monthly for 3 months.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Amongst them is the Temporary Relief Fund (TRF) to help lower and middle income Singaporeans and Permanent Residents, who have lost their jobs or experienced at least a 30% pay cut due to COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Within four days of commencing applications on 1 April 2020, more than 100,000 applications were received for the TRF support scheme.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Those who lost their jobs as a result of the economic slowdown due to COVID-19, can tap on the COVID-19 Support Grant from 1 May 2020.This grant provides assistance of $800 a month for 3 months.

sections.label: Donation amount reached $8 million
sections.summary: The donation amount has now reached more than $8 million.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: The donation amount has now reached more than $8 million.

sections.label: Couples received ROMM fee exemptions
sections.summary: In March 2020, some 49 couples received fee exemptions from ROMM.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: In March 2020, some 49 couples have received fee exemptions from ROMM.

sections.label: Malay/Muslim groups COVID-19 donations
sections.summary: PPIS will set up the PPIS WIN Fund for women in need, and the Rahmatan Lil Alamin Fund raised over $150,000 for the Courage Fund.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Another Malay/Muslim organisation that has come forward to help is the Singapore Muslim Women’s Association (PPIS) who will establish the PPIS WIN Fund for women in need and those who left their jobs to care for their aged parents or their children, during this COVID-19 situation.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: The Rahmatan Lil Alamin Fund too has also worked with the mosques to raise more that $150,000 for the Courage Fund, which I mentioned earlier.

sections.label: Ensuring wage subsidies reach workers
sections.summary: The speaker asks how wage subsidies are passed to workers, whether Government will credit them directly, and whether a Bill will mandate it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: While this Budget promises a maximum of over $3,000 per worker in wage subsidies, my question is simply how do we ensure that these subsidies are passed along to the workers?

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Does the Government intend to credit subsidies directly to our workers?

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Will we be passing a Bill mandating that employers pass these subsidies along?

sections.label: Tax deduction for IPC donations
sections.summary: The speaker suggests raising the 250% tax deduction for qualifying IPC donations, noting AWARE's reported rise in domestic violence helpline requests.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Could we also explore – in addition to the Invictus Fund that Minister Desmond Lee announced earlier – increasing the 250% tax deduction for qualifying donations made to IPCs to encourage more donations?

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: AWARE has reported a massive increase in the number of individuals seeking assistance from their domestic violence helpline.

sections.label: Pollution and smog drops
sections.summary: In China pollution dropped by over a third, and in India the smog covering cities has disappeared.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In China, pollution dropped by over a third.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In India, the smog which used to cover the cities has disappeared.

sections.label: Carbon neutral economy, working from home
sections.summary: The speaker urges the House to envision a carbon neutral economy beyond Paris Climate Agreement obligations, noting over 75% of the nation works from home.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: More than simply relying on our obligations under the Paris Climate Agreement, I urge this House to envision a carbon neutral economy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As I speak, over 75% of our nation is working from home.

sections.label: Nurses' monthly pay
sections.summary: Some nurses average only $3,000 a month despite several years of experience.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: To highlight, some of our nurses average only $3,000 a month despite several years of experience.

sections.label: Three Budgets and circuit breaker
sections.summary: The passage says to reinforce circuit breaker measures and notes three Budgets totalling $160 billion.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: It is useful for us to reinforce the importance of adhering strictly to the circuit breaker measures, but this Budget debate was originally scheduled to debate the Resilience Budget, as some Members reminded us.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: So, let us remind everyone that we should look at all three Budgets – Unity, Resilience and Solidarity, and the total allocation of $160 billion.

sections.label: WHO vaccine timeline caution
sections.summary: The WHO cautioned that a viable vaccine is at least 12 to 18 months away.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Even at its swiftest the World Health Organization (WHO) has cautioned that we are at least 12 to 18 months away from a viable vaccine.

sections.label: IMF global growth downgrades
sections.summary: The IMF downgraded its 2020 global growth forecast three times since January 2019 and expects a recession.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The IMF has downgraded its 2020 global growth forecast three times since January 2019.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The IMF is releasing a new World Economic Outlook this month and has flagged that a further downgrade is imminent.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: It expects a recession at least as bad as during the 2008 Global Financial Crisis.

sections.label: Half of humanity in lockdown
sections.summary: The passage states that half of humanity are now in lockdown.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: To achieve that, half of humanity are now in lockdown.

sections.label: Saving lives top priority
sections.summary: The passage states that saving lives and protecting Singaporeans and families is the top priority.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: In this fight against COVID-19, our top priority is saving lives, to protect Singaporeans and our families.

sections.label: Trade-off lives and economy
sections.summary: The passage states there is a trade-off between protecting lives and protecting the economy.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: In the immediate term, this is a trade-off between protecting lives and protecting the economy we must all accept – not just in Singapore, but around the world.

sections.label: Building economic and social resilience
sections.summary: The best response is to build resilience in the economy and society, the approach taken in the Resilience and Solidarity Budgets.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Our best response now is to build resilience – in our economy and society.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: That is the approach to the economic and social support in our Resilience Budget and the Solidarity Budget announced yesterday.

sections.label: Saving lives then jobs
sections.summary: Saving lives is the topmost priority, and saving jobs comes next.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: To this end, while saving lives is our topmost priority, saving jobs comes next.

sections.label: Support for wages
sections.summary: Firm failures will disrupt supply chains and drag down the economy, so high wage support is provided through the Jobs Support Scheme.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Across the economy, the failures of many firms will disrupt the supply chain and drag down the broader economy later.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Hence, we have provided high support for wages, by enhancing and extending the Jobs Support Scheme in the Resilience Budget, with a further significant enhancement for the month of April in the Solidarity Budget.

sections.label: JSS payouts reduced
sections.summary: Employers who cut wages or put employees on no-pay leave will have their JSS payouts reduced correspondingly.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: By design, employers who reduce their employees' wages or put their employees on no-pay leave during this period will have their JSS payouts reduced correspondingly.

sections.label: JSS payout disbursement
sections.summary: Firms on GIRO and PayNow receive the first JSS payout next week, cheque firms a week later, with monthly support for six months.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Firms on GIRO and PayNow will now start receiving the first JSS payout next week, while those on cheques will start receiving a week later.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: There will be support flowing every month for the next six months.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We have brought forward the scheduled due date of more than 1,000 payment vouchers, by an average of 11 days.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: This amounts to more than $600 million, benefiting close to 300 businesses, mostly SMEs.

sections.label: Passing on Property Tax Rebate
sections.summary: Property owners are legally obliged to unconditionally pass on to tenants the full Property Tax Rebate attributable to tenanted properties.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Despite these commendable moves, I have received feedback from tenants that some property owners have yet to pass on the Property Tax Rebate to them.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: This is why we are imposing a legal obligation on property owners to unconditionally pass on to their tenants the full amount of Property Tax Rebate that is attributable to the tenanted properties.

sections.label: Self-employed persons eligibility criteria
sections.summary: Revised eligibility criteria will benefit about 100,000 self-employed persons.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: With the revised eligibility criteria I announced in my Ministerial Statement, a total of about 100,000 self-employed persons will benefit.

sections.label: SATS worker redeployment
sections.summary: SATS is temporarily redeploying up to 500 workers, retrained to support the pandemic response under SG United Jobs.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: SATS is temporarily redeploying up to 500 workers who will be retrained to support our pandemic response, as part of the SG United Jobs initiative.

sections.label: SATS SpeedCargo AI trial
sections.summary: SATS, with TUM-CREATE, is trialling AI-powered cargo handling solutions through the SpeedCargo system.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: In collaboration with TUM-CREATE, SATS is trialling AI-powered solutions for cargo handling through the SpeedCargo system.

sections.label: Supply chain resilience and food security
sections.summary: Members noted COVID-19 underscored strengthening supply chain resilience and food security, including the 30 by 30 goal.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Mr Ang Wei Neng, Mr Saktiandi Supaat, Mr Gan Thiam Poh and Mr Murali Pillai have rightly pointed out that COVID-19 has underscored the importance of further strengthening our supply chain resilience and food security.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: They have urged us to press on, including on our ambitious “30 by 30” goal to develop our own food production capabilities.

sections.label: Food supplies and Budget support
sections.summary: Distributors' hard work instils confidence in food supply adequacy, and this year's Budgets support families, especially lower income.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Your hard work and that of other distributors instil confidence in the adequacy of our food supplies.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: This year’s Budgets also provide direct support for families, with more for the lower income.

sections.label: Cash support for households and workers
sections.summary: A couple with a child may receive up to $3,200 cash, Workfare workers $3,000 more, and unemployed Singaporeans a $2,400 grant.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: A 50-year old couple with a child aged 20 years old and below will receive up to $3,200 in cash.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Low-wage workers on Workfare will receive an additional $3,000 in cash to help them with their expenses over this period.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Singaporeans who become unemployed can receive the COVID-19 Support Grant of $2,400 over three months.

sections.label: Job Support Scheme wage offsets
sections.summary: Under the Job Support Scheme, employers receive up to $31,000 in wage offsets over nine months for each local worker retained.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: In addition, under the Job Support Scheme, employers will receive up to $31,000 in wage offsets over nine months, for each local worker retained.

sections.label: Solidarity Payment for adult PRs
sections.summary: Adult Permanent Residents with Singaporean parents, spouses or children may apply for a one-off $300 Solidarity Payment.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: To support these Singaporean families, adult Permanent Residents with Singaporean parents, spouses or children, may apply for a one-off Solidarity Payment of $300.

sections.label: Support package and fiscal balance
sections.summary: A support package amounting to 12% of GDP was assembled without borrowing, and self-employed persons' social security inclusion will be studied.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Our ability to put together a support package for Singaporeans amounting to 12% of GDP, without borrowing against our future, is testament to the optimal fiscal balance we have sought to maintain over the years.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: For example, as Dr Intan Mokhtar suggested, we will study whether self-employed persons should be more systematically included in our social security system.

sections.label: Fundraising from donors
sections.summary: In two months, the fund raised $1.1 million from more than 1,500 donors.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: In just two months, the fund has raised $1.1 million from more than 1,500 donors.

sections.label: Innovation, RIE 2025 and traineeships
sections.summary: Hyundai and ExxonMobil announced projects, and NRF will work with MOM on over 500 SGUnited Traineeships across the RIE eco-system.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Just last week, Hyundai announced its opening of an innovation lab in the Jurong Innovation District to develop and test technology across the automotive supply chain and trial electric vehicle manufacturing.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: In the same week, ExxonMobil also held a virtual foundation laying ceremony to deploy new technology to upgrade its integrated refining and petrochemical complex.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: This is expected to create 135 new jobs.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We will continue building smart towns like our Punggol Digital District and our efforts in deploying Autonomous Vehicles.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We are now formulating our next five-year masterplan for Research, Innovation and Enterprise, or RIE 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Under the SGUnited Traineeships Programme, NRF will work with MOM to provide more than 500 traineeships across the RIE eco-system, including our R&D labs, as well as deep-tech start-ups, accelerators and incubators.

sections.label: Emerging Stronger Task Force initiatives
sections.summary: Two initiatives will be set up: an Emerging Stronger Task Force on economic resilience and a new emphasis on social resilience.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: In this spirit, we will set up two initiatives – an Emerging Stronger Task Force on economic resilience and a new emphasis on social resilience under the Singapore Together Movement.

sections.label: Solidarity Budget spending and deficit
sections.summary: The Solidarity Budget dedicates close to $60 billion, 12% of GDP, with a record $44.3 billion deficit.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: And 11 days later, yesterday, I presented our Solidarity Budget.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We are dedicating close to $60 billion, amounting to 12% of our GDP, to deal decisively with the situation at hand.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: This is the largest spending in any financial year in our nation’s history.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We also incurred the largest deficit ever – $44.3 billion, or 8.9% of our GDP.

sections.label: President's support for reserves draw
sections.summary: The President gave in-principle support to draw up to $21 billion from past reserves for two budgets.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: In total, the President has given her in-principle support for the Government to draw up to $21 billion from our past reserves for the Resilience Budget and the Solidarity Budget.

sections.label: Reserves size and past draws
sections.summary: GIC's invested funds and total reserves are not disclosed; past draws funded 2008 and 2009 measures.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: It is the size of the funds invested by GIC that is not published.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We do not disclose the total size of our reserves for the sake of national security and strategic interests.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: They provide a key defence for Singapore in times of crisis.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: I have shared with Members that, during the 2008 Global Financial Crisis, the late President SR Nathan approved the provision of $150 billion from our past reserves to guarantee bank deposits in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: In 2009, President Nathan approved a draw of $4.9 billion from the past reserves to fund the Resilience Package then, to help us overcome the crisis.

sections.label: Possible future reserves use
sections.summary: If the crisis deepens, the economy and revenues will shrink and past reserves may be used again.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: If the crisis deepens, our economy and revenues will shrink, and we may have to make use of our past reserves again for a recovery.

sections.label: COVID-19 measures cost and deficit
sections.summary: COVID-19 measures are worth about $60 billion, 12% of GDP, with a $44.3 billion accumulated deficit.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The measures to deal with the COVID-19 outbreak is worth about $60 billion, which makes up about 12% of our Gross Domestic Product (GDP), and the accumulated fiscal deficit is $44.3 billion.

sections.label: Support schemes and reserves tap
sections.summary: Property tax rebates, Jobs Support Scheme, SIRS and Care and Support Package were introduced, with $21 billion reserves support.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: For example, in order to protect enterprises, we introduced property tax and rental rebates to help enterprises cut their cost; to protect jobs, we introduced the Jobs Support Scheme to help enterprises cope with cash flow problems and avoid retrenching their local employees.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: In addition, we have also introduced the Self-Employed Person Income Relief Scheme (SIRS) to help the self-employed.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We have also enhanced the Care and Support Package to lighten the burden of cost of living for our people.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Today, we have the ability to deal decisively with this outbreak because the Singapore Government has been saving for rainy days and practising fiscal prudence for years.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The Government has obtained in-principle support from President Halimah to tap on as much as $21 billion from our reserves.

sections.label: Trees shading and shielding
sections.summary: Trees shade on sunny days and shield from thunderstorms, enabling challenges to be dealt with without borrowing and leaving debt.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Today, these trees can not only shade us during sunny days, but also shield us from thunderstorms.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: This has enabled us to deal with the imminent challenges without having to borrow and leaving the next generation debt-laden.

sections.label: Joining frontline, three prohibitions
sections.summary: This is a critical moment to join them on the frontline, and three things must not be done: panic, go out, spread rumours.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: This is a critical moment for all of us to join them on the frontline.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We must not do three things: do not panic, do not go out and do not spread rumours.

sections.label: Businesses caring for workers
sections.summary: In the workplace, businesses should take care of their workers and retain jobs.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: In the workplace, businesses should also take care of their workers and retain jobs.

sections.label: Singapore Together and Taskforce
sections.summary: Earlier, the Singapore Together movement was launched and the Emerging Stronger Taskforce was set up.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Earlier, we launched the Singapore Together movement and set up the Emerging Stronger Taskforce.

sections.label: NIRC and spending rules
sections.summary: Spending rules exist as the Net Investment Returns Contribution, now the single largest component of spending, exceeding corporate income tax, personal income tax, GST and other taxes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: So, there are modalities to consider some of these numbers and how we can have a more deeper conversation about them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: He referred to the Business Times article and said, "Can we spend some of it to improve the livelihoods of our people?" We have our spending rules in the form of the Net Investment Returns Contribution (NIRC), and the NIRC, is as I had indicated in my previous Budget Statement is now the single largest component of spending, more than corporate income tax, more than personal income tax; in fact, more than GST and in fact, more than any other category of taxes.

sections.label: Elected Presidency checks and balances
sections.summary: The Elected Presidency involves the Auditor-General's audit and a signed letter to the President confirming whether past reserves were touched.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: And this is exactly what our Elected Presidency is about.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: And when the Auditor-General has completed his audit, I have to sign, in my name, a letter to the President, confirming whether the Government had touched the past reserves in the last Budget.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: So, the checks and balances that we have in our system have been very rigorously designed and very well observed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: I can tell you that even in presenting this Budget, when making the Government's case to the President and the Council Presidential Advisers, I spent a lot of time explaining the details and I can tell you that the President and CPA asked very, very good questions, much more than systems that I have seen elsewhere.

sections.label: COVID-19 Support Grant unpaid leave
sections.summary: A question asks whether the COVID-19 Support Grant can be extended to those on unpaid leave.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: One, can I just check whether we can extend the COVID-19 Support Grant to those who are also on unpaid leave?

sections.label: Payment to single unwed parents
sections.summary: A question asks for confirmation that the $300 given to Singaporean parents includes single unwed parents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: The last question really is can I just confirm that the $300 that we are giving out to Singapore and parents will include the single unwed parents as well.

sections.label: Arts charities Job Support Scheme eligibility
sections.summary: All charities including arts charities are eligible for the JSS if they made CPF contributions for local employees, and charity tenants in MCCY-owned properties get two months' rental waivers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: Mr Dennis Tan asked if arts charities will be eligible for the Job Support Scheme and other kinds of support they are eligible for.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: I am pleased to confirm that all charities including arts charities are eligible for the JSS as long as they have made CPF contributions for their local employees.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: All charities which are tenants in MCCY-owned properties will benefit from two months' rental waivers.

sections.label: Charities annual submissions extension
sections.summary: The Commissioner of Charities granted a three-month extension for charities' annual submissions due between 31 March 2020 and 31 July 2020.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: We understand that charities operations may be under additional strain and some have difficulties holding their AGM to finalise their financial statements.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: Therefore, the Commissioner of Charities has also granted an extension for all charities' annual submissions due during the period of 31 March 2020 to 31 July 2020, for three months.

sections.label: Mask collection conduct and total
sections.summary: The conduct was fast, efficient and safe, and more than 2.8 million masks have been collected to date.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: So, the entire conduct of this has been fast, efficient and safe.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: And to-date, more than 2.8 million masks have already been collected.

sections.label: Temporary Bridging Loan interest and risk share
sections.summary: The Temporary Bridging Loan interest rate is capped at 5%, and the Deputy Prime Minister announced 90% risk share with MAS support for banks and finance companies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
sentences.text: The Temporary Bridging Loan interest rate capped is as high as 5%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
sentences.text: But I am very grateful to hear the Deputy Prime Minister announcing risk share to 90%, and that banks and finance company will also get support from MAS with the new Singapore dollar facility.

sections.label: Support for rental flat communities
sections.summary: An MP asks Ministers to share measures supporting rental flat communities, given cramped quarters, especially during the circuit breaker month.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Can I ask one of the Ministers to share what measures are put in place to support our rental flat communities, given how cramped their quarters are as well, especially during this circuit breaker month?

sections.label: Safe distancing and housing support
sections.summary: Safe distancing applies within households; those struggling to self-isolate due to family size or environment can contact authorities for help, including additional housing support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: But it is upon the time when somebody starts to feel unwell, then you should really start to take precautions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: So, it is on that basis that safe distancing applies within the household.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Indeed, if there are members, whether in a sold flat, 3-room flat, 4-room flat or in a rental flat, if there are Singaporeans who find difficulty doing this sort of a self-isolation because of the size of their family and the physical environment that they are in, then they can contact us and we will see how best to help them including providing additional housing support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Pursuant to Standing Order 44(2), the Motion to consider the Ministerial Statement on Additional Support Measures in Response to COVID-19 Pandemic lapses at the conclusion of debate.
